PROVERB: The proverb in the targeted language/dialect
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): Explanation in targeted language (MSA for arabic dialects)
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Explanation in English (translation of the original explanation)

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 说明受压抑而反抗的部队，必然能打败敌人；骄傲的部队必定失败。比喻两者力量相当时，胜负常取决于双方各自的心态，要戒骄戒躁。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An oppressed army that fights back will surely defeat its enemy, while an arrogant army is doomed to fail. When two sides are evenly matched, the outcome often depends on their respective mindsets — one must guard against pride and rashness.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻都不够格，只能在差的人中间选择一个较好的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When none of the candidates are truly qualified, one can only pick the relatively better one from among a mediocre group.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻在不出众的人群中很难选出优秀者。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): It is very hard to select an outstanding person from a group of unremarkable people.

PROVERB: 爱跟英雄战，不爱跟狗熊斗
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻愿意与英雄战斗，不想跟懦夫较量。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One would rather fight a hero than tangle with a coward.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指古时候主帅像爱惜珍宝一样爱惜自己的将领，而对待士卒却像草一般轻视。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, a supreme commander would cherish his officers like precious treasures while treating common soldiers as worthless as grass.

PROVERB: 岸上修船易，到得江中彻底沉
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻船坏了，如果在岸上很容易修好。到了水流和风速极大的江海中，就会完全沉没。说明问题要从根本上解决，不能只做表面文章。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If a boat is damaged, it is easy to repair on shore. But once it reaches turbulent rivers and seas with strong currents and winds, it will sink completely. Problems must be solved at their root, not with superficial measures.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思指有些地方的中秋节好比过年一般热闹喜庆。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In some regions, the Mid-Autumn Festival is celebrated with as much festivity and joy as the New Year.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 簸箕星即扫帚星。迷信的人认为扫帚星的出现意味着将会发生灾祸。所以带来灾祸的人被认为就是扫帚星。比喻偶然出现的一种利益冲突。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The "dustpan star" refers to a comet. Superstitious people believed a comet's appearance foretold disaster, so anyone who brought calamity was called a "comet." This is used figuratively to describe an unexpected clash of interests.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是在很多人当中，总有一个人做领头羊。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Among a large group of people, there is always one who steps up to lead.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思为很多平凡普通的将领容易得到，但那些具有优秀领导才能的高级统帅却很难求得。亦指出类拔萃的人才稀少。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Ordinary generals are easy to find, but a truly outstanding supreme commander with exceptional leadership ability is extremely hard to come by. This also means that truly exceptional talent is rare.

PROVERB: 百里不同风，千里不同俗
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 俗是指风俗习惯。距离大约几百里，民风就大不一样；相隔干里左右，习俗就有很大差别。指各地的民风习俗差别很大。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Su" refers to customs and habits. Within a few hundred li, local customs already differ greatly; across a thousand li, traditions vary enormously. Local customs and practices differ vastly from place to place.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是筹划得再周密，也免不了会有疏漏。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter how carefully one plans, there will inevitably be some oversight.

PROVERB: 百年寿限不准有，百年计划不能无
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指人虽然不一定能够长命百岁。但不能没有长远的计划
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person may not necessarily live to be a hundred years old, but one must not be without long-term plans.

PROVERB: 百人吃百味，百里不司风
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指每人有每人的口味，每个地方也有每个地方不同的风俗习惯。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Every person has their own taste, and every place has its own distinct customs and habits.

PROVERB: 百星之明，不如一月之光
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 兀百颗星星的亮度也不能和一轮明月的光辉相比。比喻再多的普通人也不如一个核心人物的作用大。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The brightness of a hundred stars cannot compare with the radiance of a single moon. No matter how many ordinary people there are, they cannot match the influence of one key figure.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 即使胜仗连连，也不如不打仗好。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even an unbroken string of victories is not as good as not having to fight at all.

PROVERB: 百战成勇士，苦练出精兵
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是多次战斗就能磨炼出勇猛的士兵，艰苦的训练就能培养出精锐的队伍。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Numerous battles forge brave warriors, and rigorous training produces elite troops.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻吃了败仗的将领，不敢对他人讲自己的勇敢。多指人受到挫折以后，容易失去自信。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A general who has suffered defeat dares not speak of his own bravery to others. This often refers to the way people tend to lose confidence after experiencing setbacks.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指打了败仗的人没有资格再去炫耀过去的英雄事迹。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One who has lost a battle has no right to boast about past heroic deeds.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓打了败仗的将领，不值得与他共同策划天下存亡的大计。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A general who has lost his battle is not worth consulting on matters of national survival and grand strategy.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻想坑害他人，结果自己却因此吃了苦果。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One who schemes to harm others ends up suffering the bitter consequences oneself.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时推崇《论语》，认为只要运用《论语》的一半思想就能够治理好社会。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, the Analerta was so revered that people believed applying just half of its wisdom was enough to govern society well.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 陪伴君王好比陪伴老虎，随时都会招来杀身之祸。指古时君王喜怒无常。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Serving a ruler is like keeping company with a tiger — one may face mortal danger at any moment. This refers to the unpredictable temperament of ancient monarchs.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻在暗中相助的人不能露面。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person who helps from behind the scenes cannot step into the open.

PROVERB: 绑鸡的绳子，捆不住大象
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指制伏弱者的手段，不能用于制伏强者。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Methods used to subdue the weak cannot be used to subdue the strong.

PROVERB: 宝剑必付烈士，奇方必须良医
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 烈士：有志于有所建树的人。指宝剑应该给予有志之士使用，有特殊功效的药方应该出自良医之手。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Lieshi" refers to a person with ambition and aspirations. A fine sword should be given to an ambitious and worthy person, and a rare medicinal formula should come from the hands of a skilled physician.

PROVERB: 保国莫如安民，安民莫如择交
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指两国建立友好的邦交关系才能安民，安民才能保国。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only by establishing friendly diplomatic relations between nations can the people enjoy stability, and only when the people are stable can the nation be protected.

PROVERB: 备而未战，不是无战；战而无备，必有大患
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指做好准备却没有打仗，并不意味着没有战事；要打仗而准备不充分，就会导致大的灾难。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Being prepared yet not fighting does not mean there will be no war; going to war without adequate preparation will certainly lead to great disaster.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻土生土长的人或物经常受当地人歧视。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Locally grown people or products are often looked down upon by the locals themselves.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指集资容易，但合适的帮手却很难找到。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Raising capital is easy, but finding a suitable and reliable partner is hard.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻本事不大的人不可能做成大事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of limited ability cannot accomplish great things.

PROVERB: 宫逼民反民自反，君正臣廉民自安
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时认为官府腐败，就会逼得老百姓联合起来反抗；君臣清廉，老百姓自然会安居乐业。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, when officials were corrupt, the common people would be driven to unite in rebellion; when the ruler was upright and his ministers honest, the people would naturally live and work in peace and contentment.

PROVERB: 笔头尖上文官业，刀剑撑持武将威
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思为文职官员通过文章展示自己的才能，武将通过武艺树立自己的威信。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Civil officials demonstrate their talent through writing, while military generals establish their authority through martial prowess.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻两边都落空，一无所获。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Both sides end up empty — nothing is gained at all.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是有些人适合做重大的事情，而不适合承担鸡毛蒜皮小事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Some people are suited for handling important matters but not for dealing with trivial affairs.

PROVERB: 兵败如山倒，胜者似潮来
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 部队溃败好比山倒塌。指部队一旦溃败，便不可收拾如潮水一般涌上来。意为事情不可逆转。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A defeated army collapses like a mountain falling, and the victors surge forward like a tide. Once a rout begins, it is irreversible.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指打仗时可以运用欺诈的手段来迷惑对方，指挥作战的将领贵在能及时把握有利时机作战。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In warfare, deception may be freely employed to confuse the enemy; what is most valuable in a commanding general is the ability to seize the opportune moment in battle.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 兵器藏进武库，军马放入华山。意思是天下太平。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Weapons are stored in the arsenal and warhorses are released onto Mount Hua. This signifies a time of peace under heaven.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指出兵打仗，理由不正当就会吃败仗。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When an army goes to war without a just cause, it is destined to lose.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓对阵或协作的双方势均力敌。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The two opposing or cooperating sides are evenly matched in strength.

PROVERB: 兵多好打仗，人多好做活
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 兵多对作战有利，人多对干活有利。比喻人多力量大。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): More soldiers are advantageous for battle, and more hands are advantageous for work. This illustrates the power of numbers.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 用兵打仗贵在出奇制胜，而不在于人多。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In warfare, what matters is achieving victory through surprise and ingenuity, not through sheer numbers.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指用兵作战行动要快，才能让敌人出乎意料。泛指行事宜速，努力争取主动权。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Military operations must be swift to catch the enemy off guard. More broadly, any undertaking should be carried out quickly to seize the initiative.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指用兵打仗宜速战速决，不宜打持久战。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In warfare, quick decisive battles are preferable; protracted campaigns should be avoided.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时部队经过一处，就烧杀抢掠，使百姓如同蒙受一场大的火灾。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, whenever troops passed through an area, they would burn, kill, and plunder, leaving the common people as devastated as if they had suffered a great fire.

PROVERB: 兵可百年不用，不可一日不备
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 军队可以长时间不打仗，但不能一天不备战。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An army may go a long time without fighting, but it must not go a single day without being prepared for war.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指如果敌人来进犯，自有将领率而战胜方则兵迎战；如果洪水袭来，自有堤坝抵挡。也指根据不同的情况，应该采取行之有效的方法。比喻不管面临何种情况，都要有相对应的应付办法。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the enemy comes to attack, generals will lead soldiers to meet them in battle; when floodwaters come, earthen dams will hold them back. Different situations call for different effective measures. No matter what one faces, there must always be a corresponding countermeasure.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 交战时，针锋相对，抵抗敌人。比喻根据具体情况采取相对应策略。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In battle, one meets the enemy head-on in direct confrontation. This means adopting the appropriate strategy based on the specific circumstances.

PROVERB: 兵来如梳，贼来如篦，匪来如剃
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指古时的反动军队同盗贼 、土匪一样，抢劫、掠夺老百姓，各个凶残无比。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, reactionary armies were no different from bandits and outlaws — they all robbed and plundered the common people with extreme brutality.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 打仗时应该集中兵力各个击破，不宜分散。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In warfare, forces should be concentrated to defeat the enemy piecemeal, rather than being scattered.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 在军队还没有行动之前，就得先淮备好粮食和草料。指行军作战，后勤工作得先做好。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Before the troops move out, food and fodder must be prepared in advance. In any military campaign, logistics must be taken care of first.

PROVERB: 兵是将之威，将是兵之胆
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 士兵勇敢善战，才能显示将领的威风，将领有谋略，善于指挥，士兵才会勇敢过人。兵松松一个，将松松一窝士兵松散只影响个人，将领松散就会影响整个部队。意思指对将领要求更要严格。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only when soldiers are brave and skilled in battle can the general's prestige be displayed; only when the general is strategic and adept at command will the soldiers be exceptionally courageous. A slack soldier affects only himself, but a slack general affects the entire army. This means that standards for generals must be even stricter.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 士兵服从将领的命令就如草随风而动一样。比喻军令如山倒，每个士兵要服从。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Soldiers obey their general's orders just as grass bends with the wind. Military orders are absolute, and every soldier must comply.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 用兵作战没有固定的阵势，就好比水不可能有特定的形状一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Military tactics have no fixed formations, just as water has no fixed shape.

PROVERB: 兵无将而不动，蛇无头而不行
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指士兵如果没有将领的指挥，步调不可能一致，行军打仗，就如蛇没有头无法爬行一样。比喻如果没有领头人，就办不成事情。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without a general's command, soldiers cannot march in unison, just as a snake without a head cannot move. Without a leader, nothing can be accomplished.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指将领的谋略直接影响军队的强弱。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The skill or lack thereof in a commander's strategy directly determines whether the army is strong or weak.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 如果战场上没有主帅，军队就会一盘散沙。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without a commander on the battlefield, the army will fall into complete disarray.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 行军千里，即使不作战，也会疲乏。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): After marching a thousand li, an army will be exhausted even without engaging in battle.

PROVERB: 兵熊熊一个，将熊熊一窝
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 当兵的个人没本事，影响不算大，但是首领窝囊就会影响整体的战斗力。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If an individual soldier is incompetent, the impact is limited; but if the leader is incompetent, the fighting strength of the entire force is compromised.

PROVERB: 兵要练方可精，刀要磨刃才利
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是士兵只有艰苦训练，本领才能精强，就像刀要磨砺才能锋利一个道理。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Soldiers can master their skills only through rigorous training, just as a blade becomes sharp only through constant grinding.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 武器装备有好有坏，带兵打仗不可能永远都不失败。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Weapons and equipment vary in quality, and no army can win every single battle — there is no such thing as permanent victory.

PROVERB: 兵在精而不在多，将在谋而不在勇
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 士兵贵在精锐，不在于数量；主将要有谋略，不能只有勇敢。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): What matters in soldiers is quality, not quantity; what matters in commanders is strategy, not mere bravery.

PROVERB: 不打勤，不打懒，单打没长眼
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指古代衙门里的监工既不会责罚手脚麻利的工人，也不会责罚拖泥带水的工人，而是责罚那些不会察言观色的工人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient government workshops, the overseer would not punish the quick-handed worker, nor would he punish the slow one — he would only punish those who failed to read the situation and act accordingly.

PROVERB: 不当官儿不操心，不吃俸禄不担惊
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 不当朝廷的官吏就不易多操心，不拿朝廷的俸禄就不必担惊受怕，提心吊胆。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If you do not hold a government position, you need not worry about affairs of state; if you do not draw an official salary, you need not live in constant fear and anxiety.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 火候：烧火的火力强弱和时间长短。指做饭烧莱时火候不够就不能开锅。比喻做事要把握好成熟的时机，不能肓目采取行动。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Heat level" refers to the intensity of fire and the length of cooking time. If the heat is not right, one should not lift the lid. One must wait for the right moment before acting, rather than rushing in blindly.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 西天：佛经中描写的阿弥陀佛居住的地方。指不到酉天就不可能知道佛是什么样。比喻不给点颜色就不知道厉害，也比喻不身临其境就不会知道事情的来龙去脉。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The "Western Paradise" is described in Buddhist scriptures as the abode of Amitabha Buddha. Without going there, one cannot know what the Buddha is truly like. This means that without experiencing something firsthand, one cannot understand the full scope of a situation; it also means that some people do not appreciate the gravity of a situation until they are shown.

PROVERB: 不管白猫黑猫，抓住老鼠就是好猫
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是不管什么样的猫，能抓住老鼠的就是好猫。比喻不管使用什么样的方法，只要能达到最终目的就是好方法。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): It does not matter what kind of cat it is — any cat that catches mice is a good cat. It does not matter what method is used — any method that achieves the desired result is a good method.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指只有粗大结实的栋粱，才能承受得住屋架上的沉重压力。比喻只有优秀的人，才能担负起治理国家的重任。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only a thick and sturdy ridgepole can bear the heavy weight of a roof structure. Only truly capable people can shoulder the great responsibility of governing a nation.

PROVERB: 不会做饭的看锅，会做饭的看火
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 火：火候，指有利的时机。意思指不善于做饭的人总是瞅着锅里的东酉，会做饭的人却总将注意力放在火候上。比喻会办事的人总是善于把握时机。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Fire" here means the heat level, referring to favorable timing. An unskilled cook keeps watching what is in the pot, while a skilled cook keeps watching the fire. A capable person is always adept at seizing the right opportunity.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 狩猎的人看不见兔子，是不会把鹰放出去的。比喻没发现预期的目标，不到合适的时机，是不会采取行动的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A hunter does not release his hawk until he spots the rabbit. Without identifying the expected target or reaching the right moment, one does not take action.

PROVERB: 不见鱼出水，不下钓鱼竿
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻没有相当的把握，就不贸然采取行动。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without a reasonable degree of certainty, one does not rashly take action.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 佛：佛教徒称修行圆满的人。比喻遇不到合适的人就不能把自己的底细或真正的想法等说给别人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Buddha" here refers to one who has achieved spiritual perfection in Buddhist practice. One does not reveal one's true thoughts or innermost secrets unless in the presence of the right person.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是不了解对方的底细就不能随便采取行动。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without understanding the other party's true nature and background, one should not act rashly.

PROVERB: 不怕不识货，就怕货比货
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指不了解产品不用担心，只要和同类产品进行比较,就能判断出孰优孰劣。比喻无论什么事只要经过对比，就能做出正确的判断。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Not knowing the merchandise is no cause for worry — just compare it with similar products, and you can tell which is better and which is worse. Through comparison, one can always make a sound judgment about anything.

PROVERB: 不怕出山狼，就怕藏家鼠
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指从山里来的狼并不可怕，可怕的是藏在家里的老鼠。比喻潜藏的恶人比明地里的恶人更阴险，更凶恶。换句话说，潜藏在内部的恶人比明地里的恶人更可怕。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A wolf coming down from the mountains is not as frightening as a rat hiding inside one's own home. A hidden enemy within is more insidious and dangerous than an open enemy outside. In other words, internal threats are more terrifying than external ones.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 不怕官大,怕的是直接被管着指顶头上司对当事人最有约束力
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One does not fear a high-ranking official so much as the person who directly supervises you. It is your immediate superior who has the most power over you.

PROVERB: 不怕麻糖棍棍，就怕黄米包粽
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 麻糖：用麦芽糖制成的小棍状的糖果。黄米：黍子去了壳的果实，比小米稍大，黄色，煮熟后很黏。我国某些地区的风俗习惯，腊月十三要用麻糖祭灶王爷，端午节要吃用黄米和枣包成的粽子。指北方某些地方端午节后正是青黄不接的季节，穷人的日子很难过。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Matang" is a stick-shaped candy made of malt sugar. "Huangmi" is the husked grain of broomcorn millet, slightly larger than foxtail millet, yellow in color, and very sticky when cooked. In certain regions of China, matang candy is offered to the Kitchen God on the thirteenth of the twelfth lunar month, and glutinous millet dumplings with dates are eaten at the Dragon Boat Festival. In some northern areas, the period right after the Dragon Boat Festival is exactly when old grain runs out and new grain has not yet ripened — a very hard time for the poor.

PROVERB: 不怕人多心不齐，只要有人扛大旗
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 只要有威信高的人领导，大家就会积极地同心协力
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): As long as someone with high prestige takes the lead, everyone will unite and work together with enthusiasm.

PROVERB: 不怕人心似铁，难逃王法如炉
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻人的意志即使如钢铁一般坚强，也难逃如炉火一样的刑法。古时指人终将受制于王法。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter how iron-strong a person's will may be, they cannot escape the law, which burns like a furnace. In ancient times, this meant that everyone would ultimately be subject to the rule of law.

PROVERB: 不入地狱，不知饿鬼变相
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 地狱：佛教认为人死后灵魂受难的地方。饿鬼：佛教认为人生前不干好事，死后要堕入饿鬼道，饱受饥饿的痛苦。常用来比喻如果不深人对方内部，就不了解对方的底细。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Hell" is the place where the souls of the dead suffer, according to Buddhism. "Hungry ghosts" are those who, having done no good in life, fall into the Realm of Hungry Ghosts after death and endure the agony of starvation. This is commonly used to mean that without going deep inside a situation, one cannot understand the other party's true nature.

PROVERB: 不施万丈深潭计，怎得鳌鱼上钓钩
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 鳌：传说中海中的大龟或大鳖。说明没有高深的计谋就不能使有本事的人上当受骗。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Ao" refers to a legendary giant sea turtle or tortoise. Without a truly profound and cunning scheme, one cannot trick a formidable and capable person into falling for it.

PROVERB: 不图锅巴吃，不在锅边转
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 要是不想吃锅巴，就不用在锅旁边站着了。比喻由于有所目的而采取行动。也比喻为了获得利益，不得不去干这些事情。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If you do not want the crispy rice stuck to the bottom of the pot, you would not stand around the pot. People take action because they have a purpose. It also means that to obtain a benefit, one has no choice but to do certain things.

PROVERB: 不行万里路，难见痴人心
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是要经过长时间的考验，才能真正了解一个人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only through long trials and shared experiences can one truly come to know another person's heart.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 饵：钓饵，引诱鱼上钩的食物。鳌：传说中海里的大鳖。意思如果钓饵来之不义，即使鳌吞下去了，也会重新吐出来。比喻不守信义的事物，人们都会嫌弃。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Bait" refers to the lure used to hook fish. "Ao" is the legendary giant sea turtle. If the bait is obtained through unjust means, even the great sea turtle will spit it out after swallowing it. Things tainted by dishonesty and bad faith will be rejected by everyone.

PROVERB: 不用霹雳手段，显不出菩萨心肠
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 霹雳：云和地面之间发生的一种强烈雷电现象，响声巨大。比喻手段不强硬，好心肠就显不出来。又喻指恩威并济，才能达到预料目标。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Thunderbolt" refers to a violent lightning discharge between cloud and ground with a tremendous crash. Without stern and forceful measures, one's good intentions cannot be made apparent. It also means that only by combining severity with benevolence can one achieve the desired outcome.

PROVERB: 不知道他葫芦里卖的什么药
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 葫芦：古时用来装盛中药的一种器皿，又称药葫芦。指不了解对方的企图。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A "gourd" was a vessel used in ancient times to store herbal medicine, also called a medicine gourd. This means one does not understand what the other party is scheming.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 尽管出谋划策的人非常多，但最终做决定的人只有一个。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Although many people may offer advice and strategies, ultimately only one person makes the final decision.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指上天能明察善与恶，给予公平合理的奖惩。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Heaven can clearly distinguish good from evil and will bestow fair rewards and punishments accordingly.

PROVERB: 草锄不尽，终究是庄稼的害
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指不彻底铲除恶人，最终还是会给社会带来祸害。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If evildoers are not thoroughly uprooted, they will ultimately continue to bring harm to society.

PROVERB: 察见渊鱼者不祥，智料隐匿者有殃
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 察：明察，看得清楚。渊鱼：深潭中的游鱼。隐匿：隐蔽不为人所知的事。指能看清深水中游鱼的人不会有好运，能预知他人秘密的人定会招来灾难。比喻人过于聪明反受其害。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Cha" means to see clearly. "Yuanyu" means fish in a deep pool. "Yinni" means hidden, unknown matters. A person who can see the fish swimming in the depths will not have good fortune; one who can divine others' secrets will surely invite disaster. Being excessively clever brings harm upon oneself.

PROVERB: 柴多火焰高，人多声音大
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是人多力量大，就像柴多烧起来火焰高一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Strength lies in numbers, just as more firewood makes a higher flame.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 豺狼当道时肆无忌惮，没人过问，反而说起狐狸的罪过。比喻除恶要先除大害，除要害。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When jackals and wolves run rampant with impunity and no one holds them accountable, people instead point fingers at the fox. When eliminating evil, one must target the greatest threat and the most critical danger first.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 谗言会危害国家，淫妇会搅乱家庭。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Slander can endanger a nation, and a dissolute woman can throw a household into chaos.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 奉承话可以祸害国君，耿直的话才能让国家昌盛。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Flattering words can harm the ruler, while frank and honest speech can save the nation and make it prosper.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指铲除所有的邪恶不公平，国家才能安定太平。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only when all evil and injustice are completely eradicated can the nation enjoy peace and stability.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 长期被痛苦折磨，还不如一时忍受剧痛彻底解决。也指为了避开长期的麻烦，宁愿忍受眼前一时的痛苦。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Prolonged suffering is worse than enduring a brief, intense pain that resolves the problem once and for all. To avoid long-term trouble, it is better to bear a short-term hardship now.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 鹞：风筝。喻指从长计议,可以取到更大的收获。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Yao" means a kite. Taking a long-term approach and being patient can yield far greater gains.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 社稷：古时君主祭祀的土神和谷神，借指国家的政权。帝王荒淫无度，彻夜饮酒，亵渎国政，会导致国家灭亡。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Sheji" refers to the gods of earth and grain worshipped by ancient rulers, and by extension the state and its regime. A ruler who is dissolute and debauched, drinking through the night and neglecting state affairs, will bring about the downfall of the nation.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 如果自己在朝廷里面没有特殊关系的人，就不要做官。指古时做官，得有靠山。也指朝廷里面如果没有主持正义的人，就不要做官。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If you have no one with connections or influence at court, do not attempt to become an official. In ancient times, one needed a powerful backer to succeed in officialdom. It also means that if there is no one at court who upholds justice, it is better not to serve.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时指在朝廷里有后台就容易做官。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, having a powerful patron at court made it easy to obtain an official position.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 使：使用，差遣。皇帝也不差遣没吃饱的士兵去作战。指托人办事之前得先让他吃好饭或说好报酬。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Shi" means to use or dispatch. Even the emperor does not send hungry soldiers into battle. Before asking someone to do a task, one should first ensure they are properly fed or that compensation has been agreed upon.

PROVERB: 朝有奸逆，山隐草寇；国有良臣；外有忠善
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指朝内奸逆当权，英雄豪杰就只能隐居野外；国家有忠良的大臣，百姓就会忠于朝廷，安分守己。古时指社会的安定与朝廷大臣是否清廉有直接关系。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When treacherous officials hold power at court, heroes and capable people can only retreat and hide in the countryside; when the state has loyal and virtuous ministers, the common people will be faithful and law-abiding. In ancient times, social stability was directly linked to the integrity of court officials.

PROVERB: 炒豆大伙吃，炸锅一人担
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻有利益大家共同分享，有问题一个人承担。也就是说，有好处应当一起分享，遇到不好的事应当由一人承担。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When there are benefits, everyone shares them together; when problems arise, one person bears the burden alone. In other words, good fortune should be shared, while misfortune should be shouldered by an individual.

PROVERB: 车到山前必有路，船遇顶风也能开
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻事到临头自会有办法能够解决。也比喻只要奋勇前进，任何困难都能克服。常用来鼓励困难当前要坚定信心。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the moment arrives, a solution will naturally present itself. As long as one presses forward bravely, any difficulty can be overcome. This is often used to encourage people to stay confident in the face of adversity.

PROVERB: 车到山前必有路，船到桥头自然直
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻事到临头，总会有办法解决问题。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the moment comes, there will always be a way to solve the problem.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 尘世：佛教，道教指人世间。佛教中指人世间几乎没有使人开心的事情
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "The mortal world" is a term used in Buddhism and Taoism to refer to the human realm. In Buddhist thought, there are hardly any occasions for genuine happiness in the human world.

PROVERB: 称一称知轻重，量一量知短长
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指只有经过实践的检验，才可以对事情作出判别。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only through the test of practice can one properly judge a matter.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是不管事情办成功能否，得先请人喝酒。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Whether or not the matter succeeds, one must first treat the helpers to drinks.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指有做好的工艺品不能随意毁掉重作。比喻新做工艺品耗时费财。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A finished piece of craftsmanship should not be casually destroyed and redone. Making a new one from scratch is costly in both time and resources.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 秤锤虽然不大，却能称出千斤重的物体。意思是人小志气大或人物虽渺小起的作用却很大。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Although a steelyard weight is small, it can measure objects weighing a thousand jin. This means a person may be small but have great ambition, or a seemingly insignificant figure can play a very large role.

PROVERB: 秤砣小，坠千厅；胡椒小，辣人心
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是轻的能压住重的，小的能制服大的。常指不要忽视年轻人的力量。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Something light can weigh down something heavy, and something small can subdue something large. This is often used as a reminder not to underestimate the strength of the young.

PROVERB: 吃的盐和米，讲的情和理
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指做人要讲情意、讲道理。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In one's conduct, one should value both human feeling and reason.

PROVERB: 吃饭还不免掉一个米粒
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻庞大的工程难免不会出现问题。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even a massive project is bound to have some flaws.

PROVERB: 吃饭泡米汤，自己作主张
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指遇到事情自己要有主见
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When one encounters a situation, one should have one's own independent judgment.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指鱼的头部虽肉不多，但吃了鱼头肉，嘴上也沾腥。比喻干多干少担当的名声是不变的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Although a fish head has little meat, eating it still leaves a fishy smell on one's lips. Whether one does much or little, the reputation one bears remains the same.

PROVERB: 吃瓜莫吃蒂，做官莫作卑
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 吃瓜不能吃瓜蒂，因为瓜蒂是苦的；当官不能当小官，因为小官处处受制于人。古时认为当官就要当有实权的大官。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One should not eat the stem of a melon because it is bitter; one should not hold a petty office because a minor official is controlled by others at every turn. In ancient times, it was believed that if one is to hold office at all, it should be a high-ranking position with real authority.

PROVERB: 吃酒的望醉，放债的图利
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 泛指人无论做什么事，都有自己的目的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter what people do, they always have their own purpose behind it.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指不愿意占便宜的人一直站得住脚
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Those who are willing to take a loss always endure and stand firm in the long run.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 砒霜：剧毒药。比喻得不偿失。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Arsenic" is a deadly poison. This describes a situation where the cost far outweighs the gain.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻受到严厉惩处之后才了解对方的厉害，再也不敢胡作非为。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only after suffering severe punishment does one come to understand the other party's power, and one no longer dares to act recklessly.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻做了不正当的坏事就会惹祸上身。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Engaging in wrongful and improper deeds will inevitably bring trouble upon oneself.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指宁愿吃明亏，也不能吃暗亏。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One would rather suffer an open and acknowledged loss than a hidden and underhanded one.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指靠哪个行业吃饭的人，经常说的、做的就是哪个行业的事情。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Whatever trade a person relies on for a living, that trade is what they constantly talk about and engage in.

PROVERB: 吃人家的嘴软，拿人家的手短
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指吃了别人的东西，拿了别人的钱财，腰杆子就挺不起来了，遇事只能顺着别人。比喻接受了人家的宴请或礼物，就不好意思坚持公正，秉公办事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): After eating someone else's food and taking someone else's money, one can no longer stand tall — one can only go along with that person on everything. Once you have accepted someone's banquet or gift, it becomes difficult to remain impartial and handle matters fairly.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻办事总得花费点钱财。也喻指办事不付出代价是行不通的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Getting anything done always involves some expenditure. Nothing can be accomplished without paying a price.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 佛家认为，与人相处不占别人的光，会得到很多回报。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In Buddhist teaching, if one does not take advantage of others in one's dealings, one will receive much in return.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻解决问题要抓住领头人或问题的关键所在。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): To solve a problem, one must go after the ringleader or identify the crux of the matter.

PROVERB: 出门看日头，上路看风头，打铁看火头
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 出门时先看天气情况，上路行走时要观察风向，打铁时要注意火候。意指做什么事情都要善于观察，见机行事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Before going out, check the weather; before setting off on a journey, observe the wind direction; when forging iron, mind the heat. In everything one does, one should be observant and act according to the circumstances.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 打仗要乘敌人意料不到、毫无防备的时候一举击破。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In warfare, one should strike when the enemy least expects it and is completely unprepared.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指川泽之所以博深，是因为能容纳污泥浊水；山岳之所以高峻，是因为它藏得住肮脏的东西。比喻国君应该胸襟宽广，能忍辱含垢，广开言路。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Rivers and marshes are broad and deep because they can accommodate mud and foul water; mountains are tall and imposing because they can conceal blemishes within. A ruler should be broad-minded, tolerant of criticism and humiliation, and open to counsel from all sides.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 青衣：黑衣服。说明人应各为其主。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Qingyi" means black clothing. This illustrates that each person should serve their own master loyally.

PROVERB: 船有好舵手，不怕浪头高
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 只要有了好的带头人，再大的困难和风险也能克服。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): With a good leader, even the greatest difficulties and risks can be overcome.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻不论做何事，带头人是最重要的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter what the undertaking, the leader is the most important factor.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 春天不来，鲜花不会绽放。比喻时机不合适，事情就办不好。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If spring does not arrive, flowers will not bloom. If the timing is not right, things cannot be done well.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 仁慈之入不能领兵作战，仁义之人不能掌管财务
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person too kindhearted cannot command troops in battle, and a person too focused on righteousness cannot manage finances.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 纨绔：细绢做的裤子，借指富贵人家的子弟。少：少有。比喻富贵人家的子弟几乎没有能够承担重任或有所建树的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Wanku" refers to trousers made of fine silk, and by extension the sons of wealthy and noble families. "Shao" means rarely. Children of privilege and wealth rarely produce anyone who can shoulder great responsibilities or achieve anything of note.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 只要有理，辈分或地位低的人也能状告辈分或地位高的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): As long as one is in the right, a person of lower rank or status can bring a case against someone of higher rank or status.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 村子里没有大树，就只能将蓬蒿野草当做树林。意思是没有杰出的人才，只能用平庸之人代替。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If a village has no large trees, one can only regard weeds and wild grass as the forest. Without outstanding talent, one can only make do with mediocre people as substitutes.

PROVERB: 存人失地，人地皆存；存地失人，人地皆失
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 打仗时，双方力量有悬殊时，保存兵力远比收复失地要重要。也指人才在任何时候都应该放在第一位置。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When there is a great disparity in strength between the two sides in a war, preserving one's forces is far more important than recovering lost territory. Talent should always be given the highest priority.

PROVERB: 错走一步棋，满盘皆是输
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 关键时刻的一点点失误，就会功亏一箦。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A single small mistake at a critical moment can cause an entire endeavor to fail.

PROVERB: 打得一拳去，免得百拳来
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 先重击一下对方，避免他再度挑衅。也就是说，先给对方点颜色看看，让对方知道你的厉害，就可以避免对方多次重找麻烦。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Strike the opponent hard first to prevent them from provoking you again. In other words, show the opponent your strength early on so they will think twice before causing trouble repeatedly.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 打击这个人，使另外一个人也受到了惊吓。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Strike one person, and another is frightened into submission.

PROVERB: 打狗就不怕狗咬，杀猪就不怕猪叫
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻想制伏对方，就不能担忧对方报复捣乱。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If you want to subdue an opponent, you cannot be afraid of their retaliation.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 惩罚一个人要考虑到主子或与他有关的人的颜面。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When punishing someone, one must consider the face and dignity of that person's master or those associated with them.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 惩罚一个人，要考虑到与他有某种关系的人的情面。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When punishing someone, one must take into account the feelings of those who have a certain relationship with that person.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指降伏普通的敌人时，也不能轻敌，要拿出对付最凶狠敌人的办法和力量。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even when dealing with an ordinary enemy, one must not be careless — one should bring the same effort and strategy used against the fiercest of foes.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻没有除害，反而自己受到伤害。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Instead of eliminating the threat, one ends up being harmed oneself.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指处理问题只要抓住了关键就会迎刃而解。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Once you seize the key to a problem, everything else falls into place with ease.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是打击凶狠的敌人要小心防范敌人反扑。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When striking a fierce enemy, one must be careful to guard against a counterattack.

PROVERB: 打虎进深山，捕蛇下箐底
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 箐：竹木丛生的山谷。比喻办事情要找对门路。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Qing" refers to a mountain valley thick with bamboo and trees. One must find the right approach to get things done.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻要降服强敌，必须先消灭其最主要的依靠力量。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): To subdue a powerful enemy, one must first eliminate the main force on which that enemy depends.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是双方发生争斗时应先发制人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When a fight breaks out, the one who strikes first gains the advantage.

PROVERB: 打人休打脸，骂人休揭短
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 与他人发生争斗时，应考虑到对方的颜面。又指要给他人留些脸面不要揭他人的短处。打人一拳，防人一脚防备敌人的回击。说明在进击敌人时，要谨防敌方反扑.
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When in conflict with another person, one should consider the other's dignity. One should also leave others some face and not expose their weaknesses. After throwing a punch, be ready to block a kick — when attacking the enemy, one must guard against a counterattack.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 打蛇没有打死它，就会自留祸害。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If you strike a snake but fail to kill it, you leave trouble for yourself.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 七寸： 蛇的要害之处。比喻降敌得攻其要害，做事得抓住关键。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Seven inches" refers to the vital spot of a snake. To defeat an enemy, one must attack the critical weakness; to accomplish anything, one must seize the key point.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 打蛇要先打靠近蛇头部的方位。意思指与敌人交战时要先攻其要害。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When striking a snake, aim first near its head. When engaging an enemy, attack the most vital point first.

PROVERB: 打蛇先打头，擒贼先擒王
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指要想降服敌人，先要擒拿他们的领头人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): To subdue the enemy, first capture their leader.

PROVERB: 打死胆大的，吓死胆小的
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 惩治胆大的，胆小的自然会收敛。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Punish the bold offender, and the timid ones will naturally restrain themselves.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻镇压首恶，帮凶就不会胡作非为。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Suppress the ringleader, and the accomplices will no longer dare to act recklessly.

PROVERB: 打天下时靠人才创业，坐天下时用奴才享乐
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时指打天下需要有志之士的帮助，坐天下则需要奴才逢迎侍奉。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, conquering the realm required the help of ambitious and capable people, but ruling the realm required obedient servants to attend and flatter.

PROVERB: 打铁要趁热，治病要趁早
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 办事要把握合适的时机，及时采取行动。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One must seize the right moment and act in a timely manner.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻软硬兼施，先使其受挫，再示以扰慰。换句话说，先打击敌方，杀去威风，让敌方服输了，然后再拉拢他。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Use both hard and soft tactics — first deal a blow to break their spirit, then extend a gesture of goodwill. In other words, first strike the enemy and humble them into submission, then win them over.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思指力强的人欺负弱小的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The strong bully the weak.

PROVERB: 大虫欺小虫，蚱蜢欺蝗虫
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻强势的人总是欺凌弱小的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Those who hold power always oppress the powerless.

PROVERB: 大胆天下去得，小心寸步难行
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 胆大的人能够闯天下走四方，胆小怕事的人却迈不开笫一步。劝诫人做事情不要前怕狼后怕虎，过分谨慎小心。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The bold can venture forth and conquer the world, while the timid cannot even take the first step. One should not be overly cautious, fearing danger at every turn.

PROVERB: 大盗沿街走，无赃不定罪
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 没有赃物作证据，就不能随便给比喻他人定罪名。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without stolen goods as evidence, one cannot casually convict another person.

PROVERB: 大佛三百五，各有成佛路
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻每个人做事有每个人的办法手段。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Every person has their own way of doing things.

PROVERB: 大缸里打翻了油，沿路儿拾芝麻
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指丢弃大的捡拾小的，得不偿失。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Discarding something large to pick up something small is a losing bargain.

PROVERB: 大官不要钱，不如早归田；小官不索钱，儿女无姻缘
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指古时不论官职大小，官员都要榨取百姓的血汗钱。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, officials of every rank, high or low, would squeeze the common people for their hard-earned money.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻大家的东酉，大家应当共同享用。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): What belongs to everyone should be shared and enjoyed by everyone.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 奸佞诡诈的人，往往装出忠诚老实的模样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Treacherous and deceitful people often put on an appearance of loyalty and honesty.

PROVERB: 大将保明主，俊鸟登高枝
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻优秀的人才愿意到最能发挥自己才华的地方去施展才能。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Outstanding talent gravitates to the place where it can best be put to use.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 做领导的如果没有才干，人们就会跟着受苦受累。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When those in charge lack ability, everyone under them suffers.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指将军不需要在前线冲锋陷阵，只要在后边压阵指挥就可以了
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A general does not need to charge into the front lines; it is enough to command and hold the rear.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指只看见小处，看不到大处，眼光短浅。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Seeing only the small picture while missing the big one — this describes a person of narrow and short-sighted vision.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时的观念认为遭遇了大灾难而不死，日后一定会有所作为。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The ancient belief held that a person who survives a great calamity is destined to accomplish great things in the future.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是人的气量大，胸怀广阔能宽容人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of great magnanimity and broad mind can be tolerant and forgiving of others.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 遭遇过重大冤屈的人必定有申冤及施展抱负的机会。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One who has suffered a grave injustice will surely have the chance to clear their name and fulfill their ambitions.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指地位高的人不会念叨地位低的人犯的过错。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of high status does not dwell on the faults of those beneath them.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时认为读书人固执迂腐，优柔寡断，不能够与之共谋大事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, it was believed that scholars were stubborn, pedantic, and indecisive, and therefore unfit to be consulted on important undertakings.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻只要有靠山在，附庸者自然平安无事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): As long as the great tree stands, those sheltered beneath it will naturally be safe and sound.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 大树底下树荫多，是乘凉的好地方。意思是有长辈或有权势者的庇护，就能过上好日子。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Under a great tree there is ample shade — a fine place to cool off. With the protection of an elder or a person of power, one can live comfortably.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 1，遮阴面积大的树下是乘凉的好地方。2，比喻有大的势力作垫后，办事就容易。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): First, a tree with broad shade is a good place to rest. Second, with a powerful backer behind you, everything becomes easier to accomplish.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 大树下面的小草由于有树叶的遮挡霜打不到。意思指在有权势者的保护下不会受到侵害。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The grass beneath a great tree is shielded from frost by the canopy of leaves. Under the protection of the powerful, one will not be harmed.

PROVERB: 大水未到先治坝，休到河边再脱鞋
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 在问题浮现之前，就要想好对付的措施。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Before problems surface, one should already have countermeasures in mind.

PROVERB: 大水淹了龙王庙，一家人不认识一家人
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 龙王管水，自己的庙却被水淹没。意谓一家人之间产生误会或内部出现矛盾冲突。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The Dragon King governs the waters, yet his own temple gets flooded. This refers to misunderstandings or conflicts arising within one's own family or organization.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 阎罗王容易见，小鬼最难缠。意谓首领往往好说话，而其手下的人常常不好对付。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The King of Hell is easy to deal with, but his petty demons are the real nuisance. The person at the top is often reasonable, while those beneath them are the ones who are difficult to handle.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 从大象嘴里拔牙。意谓触犯势力强大的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Pulling a tooth from an elephant's mouth — this means provoking or offending someone of great power.

PROVERB: 带箭野猪猛于虎，老鼠急时会咬人
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻受到重创后的敌人，为了逃命，会凶悍无比，因此要谨慎小心严加防范。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An enemy that has been gravely wounded becomes ferociously desperate in its attempt to escape, and therefore one must be especially vigilant and cautious.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻只有付出一定的代价才能如愿以偿。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only by paying a certain price can one get what one wishes for.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 胆小怕事的人不足以领兵打仗。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person who is timid and fearful is not fit to lead troops into battle.

PROVERB: 当差的官面上看气，行船的看风使篷
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 下级要看上级的脸色行事，就好比行船时要见风使舵一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A subordinate must read the superior's mood and act accordingly, just as a boatman adjusts the sails to the wind.

PROVERB: 当官不为民做主，不如回家卖红薯
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 当官就要给为民办事，否则不如辞官回家。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If you hold office, you should serve the people; otherwise, you might as well resign and go home.

PROVERB: 当官的动动嘴，当兵的跑断腿
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 上级领导一句话，属下就忙得团团转。常用来讽刺官僚主义作风。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A single word from a superior sends all the subordinates scrambling. This is often used to satirize bureaucratic behavior.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指下棋的人容易糊涂，围观的人却反而看得一清二楚。也指当事人容易头脑发晕，考虑不周；局外人却头脑清醒，看得真切。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The chess player easily gets confused, while the onlooker sees the game clearly. The person directly involved tends to lose perspective and think poorly, while an outsider, with a clear head, sees everything as it truly is.

PROVERB: 当权若不行方便，如入宝山空手回
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指掌权的人如果为别人提供不了便利，就如同进了宝山又空手而归一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If a person in power cannot offer any convenience or benefit to others, it is like entering a mountain of treasure and coming away empty-handed.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 公堂之上，即使是做父亲的也得秉公办事。指法不容私。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In a court of law, even a father must handle matters impartially. The law allows no room for personal favoritism.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是每时每刻都处于高度的戒备状态。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): To be in a state of the highest vigilance at every moment.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 双方在冲突中针锋相对，格袼不入，拼得你死我活。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The two sides are locked in fierce, unyielding confrontation — a fight to the death with neither giving an inch.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 官位是靠作战立功谋取得到的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Official rank is earned through military merit and distinguished service in battle.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 灵山：佛祖居住的圣地，泛指佛地。比喻好人好事无处不在。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Lingshan" is the sacred place where the Buddha resides, and by extension refers to any holy Buddhist site. Good people and good deeds can be found everywhere.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 道：道行,指佛家修行的功夫。魔：魔罗的略称，佛教指破坏修行的恶魔，如烦恼、疑惑、迷恋等。本为佛家语，告诫修行者必须小心世俗的诱惑。比喻取得成功之后，前进的道路上可能会有更大的拦路虎。也比喻总有压倒或打败对方的一着。还比喻正义总能打败邪恶。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Dao" refers to the level of spiritual cultivation in Buddhism. "Mo" is short for "Moluó," meaning the evil demons in Buddhism that obstruct spiritual practice — such as vexation, doubt, and worldly attachment. Originally a Buddhist term warning practitioners to guard against worldly temptation. It is used figuratively to mean that after achieving success, even greater obstacles may lie ahead on the road forward. It also means that for every powerful move, there is always a counter-move. It further illustrates that justice will always triumph over evil.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 符合道义的人昌盛，违背道义的人衰亡。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Those who follow righteousness will prosper; those who defy it will perish.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指自己有理就不愿让步。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When one is in the right, one refuses to yield.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 占便宜了，还要卖弄自己的小聪明。意思是既得到了好处，又把话说得冠冕堂皇。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Having already taken the advantage, one still shows off one's cleverness — gaining the benefit while making it all sound perfectly noble and justified.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 在政权的夺取中，得到人们真心拥护的一方就能夺得政权。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In the struggle for political power, the side that wins the genuine support of the people will prevail.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 得民心者昌盛，失民心者衰亡。指民心向背是决定兴亡的关键因素。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Those who win the hearts of the people will flourish; those who lose them will fall. The allegiance of the people is the decisive factor in determining rise or ruin.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指得到好处随即就得溜走，不能沉湎其中。比喻做事要知足，要适可而止，该抽身时就抽身，功成身退。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Once you have gained the advantage, you should withdraw promptly and not linger. One should know when enough is enough, stop while ahead, and retire after success.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻对别人的问题看得很透彻，但对自己就没有自知之明。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One can see through other people's problems with great clarity, yet lacks self-awareness about one's own shortcomings.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指地方官府权势比较大，判定的结论不容易改变。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Local authorities wield considerable power, and their rulings are not easily overturned.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指双方都十分强硬。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Both sides are equally unyielding and refuse to back down.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指手中没有木棍，狗就会来咬你。换句说话，人不能放弃自卫的权力，要不然就会受欺负。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without a stick in your hand, the dog will come and bite you. In other words, one must not give up the right to self-defense, or one will be bullied.

PROVERB: 东山的老虎吃人，西山的老虎也吃人
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指坏人的本质都是相同的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): All bad people share the same nature at heart.

PROVERB: 东庄的土地到西庄不灵
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻权力不在管辖范围之内就不起作用。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Authority has no effect outside its own jurisdiction.

PROVERB: 动了太岁头上土，无灾也有祸
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时认为太岁之神在地，如果要动土，就得避开太岁的方位，要不然就会遭受祸害。意指触犯了有权势的人会遭受祸害。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, it was believed that the god Taisui resided underground, and anyone digging earth had to avoid his position or suffer calamity. This means that offending a powerful person will bring disaster upon oneself.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻做人只要磊落光明，什么诽谤也不用怕。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): As long as one is open and upright, one need not fear any slander.

PROVERB: 肚里没冷病，不怕吃西瓜
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻不做亏心事，就不担心外人的闲言碎语。也比喻自己行为正派不做坏事，就不担心外人的批评和议论。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If one does nothing to trouble one's conscience, one need not worry about gossip from others. If one's conduct is upright and one commits no wrongdoing, one need not fear criticism or comment from outsiders.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 跟不识字的人讲话，要避开文雅的话题。比喻说话要看对象，要因人而异。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When speaking with an illiterate person, one should avoid literary or highbrow topics. One should tailor one's speech to the audience.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 用来讥笑说话不看对象的人。比喻讲话不看对象，对愚人讲深奥的道理就会毫无意义。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): This is used to mock those who do not consider their audience when speaking. Expounding profound principles to someone who cannot understand them is utterly pointless.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指多一件事物就多一些烦恼。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Every additional thing one acquires brings additional worries.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指尽力多多获取。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Try to obtain as much as possible.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指龙多了反而互相推诿，谁也不施雨。比喻人多了做事的效率反而会降低。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When there are too many dragons, they pass the responsibility to one another and none brings rain. When there are too many people involved, efficiency actually decreases.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 多做谋划一定能胜过少做谋划的。也就是说，凡事应多考虑。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): More planning will always prevail over less planning. In all matters, one should think things through carefully.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 打仗靠的是计谋而不是人数，意指智取优于力取。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Wars are won by strategy, not by numbers — outwitting the enemy is superior to overpowering them.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指和尚能躲过，和尚住的寺院却躲不过。也指出现了问题，当事人逃了，但事体依然还在。即无论如何也逃脱不掉。换句话说，虽然暂时可以逃避，但最终还是得面对。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The monk can hide, but the temple cannot. When trouble arises, the person involved may flee, but the matter itself remains. There is ultimately no escape. Although one may avoid something temporarily, one must face it in the end.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指恶人都欺软怕硬，要敢于同恶人斗争到底。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Evil people bully the weak and fear the strong — one must dare to fight them to the very end.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是再凶猛的老虎也打不过钻进肚子里的蛇。比喻内部的对手是心腹之患，是最难对付的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter how fierce a tiger may be, it cannot defeat a snake that has burrowed into its belly. Internal enemies are the most dangerous, for they are the hardest to guard against.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻恶人会有更凶恶的人来制伏他。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): For every wicked person, there is someone even more ruthless who will bring them to heel.

PROVERB: 饿急了吃五毒，渴急了喝盐卤
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 五毒：旧时称蝎子，蛇、壁虎、蜈蚣和蜘蛛为五种毒虫。比喻遇到急事便由不得自己选择。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The "five venomous creatures" in old times referred to scorpions, snakes, geckos, centipedes, and spiders. When faced with an urgent matter, one has no luxury of choice.

PROVERB: 饿了来馒头，困了遇枕头
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指所希望的所需要的，得到了满足或实现。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): What one hopes for and needs has been fulfilled or realized.

PROVERB: 罚不择骨肉，赏不避仇雠
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 骨肉：指父母、兄弟、子女等亲人。雠：对手，仇雠即仇人。惩罚的时候，不考虑是否是亲人；奖赏的时候，不考虑是否是仇人。指赏罚应一视同仁，不分亲疏远近。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Flesh and bone" refers to parents, siblings, children, and other close kin. "Chóu" means adversary or enemy. When meting out punishment, one does not consider whether the person is a relative; when bestowing rewards, one does not consider whether the person is a foe. Rewards and punishments should be applied impartially, without regard to closeness or distance of relationship.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓法律不能制裁大多数人，只能制裁少部分人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The law cannot punish the majority — it can only punish the few.

PROVERB: 法律不能松，松了乱哄哄
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓建立健全的法制十分重要要不然社会秩序就会混乱。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Establishing a sound legal system is of the utmost importance; otherwise, social order will descend into chaos.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 天道的祛网，看起来虽然稀疏，但实际上不会漏掉任何一个作恶多端的人。比喻作恶者终究会受制于法。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The net of Heaven's justice appears loose and wide-meshed, yet in truth it lets no evildoer slip through. Those who commit evil will ultimately be brought to justice.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指法令难以完美无缺。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Laws and statutes can never be entirely flawless or perfect.

PROVERB: 法无三日严，草是年年长
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 执法经常是开始严格后来松懈罪犯却往往像青草一样不断滋生。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Law enforcement is often strict at first but grows lax over time, while criminals keep springing up endlessly like wild grass.

PROVERB: 法正天心顺，官清民自安
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 执法公正，老天也会顺应；为官清廉，百姓自然平安无事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the law is enforced justly, Heaven itself responds favorably; when officials are incorruptible, the people naturally live in peace.

PROVERB: 法字没多重，万人抬不动
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 法律制度庄严神圣，不可动摇，无论是谁都必须遵守。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The legal system is solemn and sacred, unshakable — everyone, without exception, must abide by it.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指暗中陷害人比猛虎害人还不容易防范。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person who harms others in secret is even harder to guard against than a man-eating tiger.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指不论什么制度和措施对那些一心作乱的小人来说，都很难有约束力。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter what system or measure is put in place, it is nearly impossible to restrain those petty villains who are bent on making trouble.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 把渔竿上的线放得长长的，期望可以钓到大鱼。意指策划周密，引出深藏的、关键的敌人，以求更大的收获。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Let the fishing line out long, in hopes of catching a big fish. This means to plan carefully and patiently, drawing out a deeply hidden and critical enemy in order to achieve a greater gain.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指放走了强敌，日后必然会造成大祸患。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Letting a powerful enemy escape will inevitably lead to great disaster in the future.

PROVERB: 飞沙再大也遮不住牧人的眼睛
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 风沙再大也遮挡不了牧人灵敏的双眼。意指政治目光锐敏的人有能力分辨清楚错综复杂的问题。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter how fierce the sandstorm, it cannot blind the keen eyes of the herdsman. A person with sharp political insight has the ability to see clearly through the most tangled and complex of situations.

PROVERB: 非理之财莫取，非理之事莫为
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指违背情理的钱财不可以获取，违背情理的事情不可以去做。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Money gained against reason and conscience should not be taken; deeds that violate propriety and justice should not be done.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻不让别人沾自己的光。换句话说，好处或便宜不能让外人给白白得去了。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Not letting others benefit from one's own advantage. In other words, one should not allow outsiders to freely enjoy benefits that belong to oneself.

PROVERB: 风吹鸡蛋壳，财去人安乐
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指没有钱财，人的生活反而会轻松。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without wealth, a person's life is actually lighter and more carefree.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指遇到大风，贴近墙根走。比喻遇到强敌，可暂时回避一下。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When a great wind blows, walk close to the base of the wall. When facing a powerful enemy, one may temporarily step aside and avoid direct confrontation.

PROVERB: 逢桥须下马，过渡莫争先
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指过桥时要下马步行，渡河时不能争先上船。比喻外出行走要时刻注意安全，碰到危险要采取防范措施。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Dismount when crossing a bridge; do not rush to board a boat when crossing a river. When traveling, one must always be mindful of safety and take precautions when encountering danger.

PROVERB: 佛门虽大，难度无缘之人
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 度：僧尼引导俗人出家。没有佛缘的人不容易成为信徒。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Dù" means for a monk or nun to guide a layperson into monastic life. A person without karmic affinity with the Buddha will not easily become a devotee.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 刘禅虽然有诸葛亮的扶持，但仍没有保住刘备打下的江山。意指碌碌无为的庸人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Although Liu Shan had the support of Zhuge Liang, he still could not preserve the empire that Liu Bei had won. This refers to a mediocre and incompetent person who accomplishes nothing of value.

PROVERB: 腐木不可以为柱，卑人不可以为主
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 不能用腐朽的木材做房屋的柱子，不能让地位低下的人来主事。指让卑微的人主事有可能坏事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Rotten wood cannot be used as a pillar for a house, and a person of low standing should not be put in charge of important affairs. Placing someone unfit in a position of authority may ruin everything.

PROVERB: 妇女能顶半边天，离了妇女没吃穿
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指妇女的能力和贡献与男子一样大，离开妇女很多事情办不成。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Women's abilities and contributions are equal to those of men — without women, many things simply cannot be accomplished.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指人富贵了，有了权势，不应该欺压自己的乡亲。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When a person gains wealth and power, they should not use it to bully their own fellow villagers and neighbors.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻没出力却捡了个大便宜。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Not having contributed any effort, yet picking up a great bargain. This describes someone who profits without doing any work.

PROVERB: 钢刀虽快，不斩无罪之人
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指国家的法律虽然严格，但也不会处罚无罪之人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Although a nation's laws are strict, they will not punish an innocent person.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 诬告别人犯死罪的人，自己也得死罪。意谓告状这种事责任重大，应当非常慎重。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One who falsely accuses another of a capital crime shall themselves receive the death penalty. Filing a lawsuit is a matter of grave responsibility and should be approached with the utmost caution.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指鸽子愿意到人烟兴旺的地方去。比喻古时势利人都愿意攀附有钱有势的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Pigeons prefer to go where there are thriving settlements. In ancient times, opportunistic people always sought to attach themselves to the wealthy and powerful.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 行：行业。指行业不同，但道理一样、相通。换句话说，行业虽然不一样，但基本事理和规律却是相差无几的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Háng" means trade or profession. Though trades differ, the underlying principles are the same. In other words, although industries may vary, the fundamental logic and patterns are much alike.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指个人利益要服从国家利益。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Individual interests must be subordinated to the interests of the state.

PROVERB: 各处各乡俗，一处一规矩
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是不同的地方都有各自不同的风俗习惯和规矩。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Different places each have their own distinct customs, habits, and rules.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 每个人都在打自己的算盘。意指各人都在盘算各自的利益。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Everyone is working their own abacus. Each person is calculating their own interests.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指各人做事各人自己受益。比喻自己动手做事，自己先受益。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Each person does their own work and reaps their own benefit. Do it yourself and you are the first to benefit.

PROVERB: 耕牛无宿草，仓鼠有余粮
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指辛苦劳作却一无所有，不费力气却生活富裕。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Those who toil bitterly have nothing, while those who exert no effort live in comfort.

PROVERB: 公道不公道，自有天知道
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓办事公正与否，无人知晓。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Whether something is handled fairly or not, no one really knows.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指不论什么事大家自有公正的评判。换句话说，公正的道理本身就在大家的心里，是非曲直自有公论。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The public will always render a fair judgment on any matter. In other words, the sense of justice resides in everyone's heart, and right and wrong will ultimately be determined by public opinion.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时认为在衙门中干事的人容易行善。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, it was believed that those who worked in government offices had easy opportunities to do good deeds.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 差役看见老百姓手里的财物，就像苍蝇看见血一样。意指古时的差吏敲诈勒索百姓，贪婪成性。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Government runners eye the common people's possessions the way flies are drawn to blood. In ancient times, petty officials extorted the populace and were insatiably greedy.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 公正才能廉明，廉洁才会有威望。意思是做官应该公正廉洁。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Fairness leads to integrity, and integrity earns respect. An official should be just and incorruptible.

PROVERB: 公则民不敢慢，廉则吏不敢欺
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 公正，老百姓就不敢怠慢；廉洁，属吏就不敢欺诈。指做官一定要清正廉洁。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When an official is fair, the people dare not be negligent; when an official is clean, subordinates dare not cheat. One who holds office must be upright and incorruptible.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 大家的马，大家都有权力骑。意指公共财物大家都可以享用。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A communal horse may be ridden by all. Public property may be enjoyed by everyone.

PROVERB: 功者难成而易败，时者难得而易失
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 建功立业困难而失败却很容易，抓住机会艰难而失去机会更容易。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Achieving success is difficult while failure comes easily; seizing opportunity is hard while losing it is effortless.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 敌人毫无防备时进攻，敌人预料不到时出击。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Attack when the enemy is unprepared; strike when the enemy least expects it.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 恭敬谦让，不如服从。意指在别人赠送礼物或请去吃饭时，应以听从主人的意见最好。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Rather than being overly polite and deferential, it is better simply to comply. When someone offers a gift or extends an invitation, the best course is to graciously accept the host's wishes.

PROVERB: 狗肉上不得台盘，稀泥巴糊不上壁
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指狗肉档次不高，上不了宴席；稀泥不够黏，糊不到墙壁上。比喻素质低的人不值得抬举或见不了世面。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Dog meat is too lowly for a banquet table; thin mud is too weak to stick to a wall. A person of poor quality cannot be elevated or presented in polite society.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 姑：此处指婆婆。妇：此处指儿媳。指婆婆的嘴如果整天唠叨个不停，媳妇的耳朵也就听腻了。也比喻如果领导说话太絮烦了，属下就会充耳不阐。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Gū" here refers to the mother-in-law; "fù" refers to the daughter-in-law. If the mother-in-law nags endlessly, the daughter-in-law's ears grow numb to it. Likewise, if a leader talks too much, subordinates will simply stop listening.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 关公为武将，在他眼前耍弄大刀肯定是自不量力。意指在行家面前卖弄本领，班门弄斧。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Guan Gong was a great warrior — to brandish a broadsword before him is sheer overconfidence. This means showing off one's skills before a master, like playing an axe before Lu Ban's door.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 关节：指古时暗中行贿买通官吏。阎罗：迷信者称之为管地狱的神。包老：包拯，北宋丞相。指包公立场刚毅，为官清正，关节也买不通。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Guānjié" refers to secretly bribing officials in ancient times. "Yánluó" is the god said to rule the underworld. "Bāo Lǎo" is Bao Zheng, the Northern Song chancellor. Bao Zheng was so firm in principle and upright in office that no bribe could ever sway him.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时认为官府腐败，逼得老百姓无路可投，只能群起反抗。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, it was believed that when the government became so corrupt that the common people had nowhere to turn, they had no choice but to rise up in rebellion.

PROVERB: 官逼民反民自反，君正臣廉民自安
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指官府逼迫压榨，把老百姓都逼上了死路，老百姓就会起来反抗；国君清明公正，大臣们都廉洁奉公，老百姓就会安居乐业。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the government oppresses and squeezes the people until they have no way out, the people will revolt. When the sovereign is wise and just and officials are clean and dutiful, the people will live and work in peace and contentment.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 做官的不差遣身体不适的人外出办事。意指在工作上要适当考虑身体不好的人的处境。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An official does not send an ailing person out on errands. One should give due consideration to those in poor health when assigning work.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指做官的人不会威逼已经顺从了的老百姓。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An official does not coerce people who have already submitted and complied.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 做官的官印不能脱手，做生意的货物不能离身。意指必须看管好自己借以谋生的物品。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An official must not let go of their seal of office; a merchant must not be separated from their goods. One must guard carefully whatever one depends upon for a livelihood.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指如果按照国法办事，类似于小针般的违法行为也不能宽容；如果徇私舞弊，对再严重的犯法罪行也能网开一面。讽喻古时官吏大多贪赃受贿，私情大于国法。比喻官场中办事没有通融的余地，人们私下交涉变通的可能性却更大。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If matters are handled strictly by national law, even the slightest infraction cannot be pardoned; if personal connections are used, even the gravest crime can be overlooked. This satirizes how ancient officials mostly accepted bribes and let private relations override the law. In official channels there is no room for flexibility, yet through back channels almost anything can be negotiated.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指官府依法办事，极小的违法之举也不能容许；私下办事，再严重的违法行为都能通融。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the government enforces the law, even the smallest violation cannot be tolerated; when matters are handled privately, even the most serious offenses can be accommodated.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指官职再大也比不上直接经管的人权力大。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter how high one's official rank, it cannot compare to the power of the person who directly manages the matter at hand.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 当官的不贪图钱财，其手下的士兵就不畏惧死亡。意指做领导的人要起到身先士卒的表率作用。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When those in command are not greedy for money, the soldiers beneath them will not fear death. Leaders must set an example by leading from the front.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 为官的不修理衙门，住店的客人不整理店房。意思是苟且度日，没有长远规划。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Officials do not repair their offices, and inn guests do not tidy their rooms. This describes a mentality of muddling through without any long-term planning.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 为公家办事，不能自己说了算。意指做事情要服从上级的安排。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When handling public affairs, one cannot make decisions unilaterally. One must follow the arrangements of one's superiors.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指不管官差有多大差错，被差遣来办事的人本身是没有过错的。官大一品压死人指古时官职大的官吏可以借助手中权力欺压下级。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter how great the error of an official order, the messenger who carries it out bears no fault. A superior who outranks you by even one grade can crush you — in ancient times, higher-ranking officials could use their power to oppress their subordinates.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指古时官职越高的人，越是飞扬跋扈，目中无人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, the higher one's official rank, the more arrogant and overbearing one became, regarding no one as an equal.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指古时官职大的官吏可以借助手中权力欺压下级。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Officials of higher rank could use the power in their hands to oppress those below them.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 官：指衙门官吏。断：决断，判定案子。十：众多的意思。指官府审案有多种方法。比喻官员判定官司，需要迎合相关上司的意图。这是旧官吏遵守的官场规则，也是古时造成冤假错案的主要原因。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Guān" refers to government officials. "Duàn" means to render judgment on a case. "Shí" here means many or various. The government has many methods for trying cases. Officials deciding lawsuits must cater to the intentions of their relevant superiors. This was the unwritten rule officials followed, and it was also the main cause of unjust and wrongful verdicts in ancient times.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指国家的法律容不得讲任何的情面。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The law of the land allows no room for personal sentiment or favoritism.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指为官的清正廉洁，社会风气就会清明。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When those in office are upright and incorruptible, the moral atmosphere of society will be clear and bright.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 即使是官府也不会殴打为他送礼的人。泛指不应该令淡对自己示好的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even a government office would not beat someone who comes bearing gifts. One should never mistreat those who show goodwill toward oneself.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 无论做什么事都应该有一定的文字凭证。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Whatever one does, there should always be written documentation as proof.

PROVERB: 官清民自安，法正天心顺
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 一个国家当官的如果清正廉洁法律严正，老百姓就能够顺心安定。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When a nation's officials are upright and its laws are strictly enforced, the common people can live in peace and contentment.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时认为官场势利，容不得讲人情。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, it was believed that officialdom was driven by self-interest and left no room for personal sentiment.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是在官场上办事，要学会随时事的变化而改变自己的计划。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In the world of officialdom, one must learn to adapt one's plans as circumstances change.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 公家的土砌公家的墙。意指公款办公事，专款专用。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Public clay builds the public wall. Public funds should be used for public business — earmarked money for earmarked purposes.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时官场办案经常是前紧后松，草率了事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, official cases were often handled with initial urgency that quickly tapered off, ending in a hasty and perfunctory conclusion.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是古时私设公堂所用的刑罚要比官府的刑罚残酷很多，无法让人忍受。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, the punishments inflicted in private, extralegal courts were far more cruel and unbearable than those of the official government.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指官场中若没有有权势的人作靠山，就做不长官。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In officialdom, without a powerful patron to back you, you will not remain in office for long.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 光棍：方言，聪明人。指聪明人在形势不利时要妥协让步。换句话说，聪明人在处于劣势的情况下暂时妥协让步，应该先避免吃眼前亏，然后另谋对策。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Guānggùn" is a dialectal term for a clever person. A clever person knows when to compromise and yield in unfavorable circumstances. In other words, a smart person in a position of weakness will temporarily concede to avoid immediate loss, and then devise a new strategy.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是对败退的敌人不要袭击，对无路可退的残敌不要往死里追赶，谨防其反扑，做垂死挣扎。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Do not attack a retreating enemy; do not pursue a cornered remnant force to the death. Beware of their desperate counterattack in a final struggle for survival.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 地位高的人不记得琐碎小事多用作客套或奉承话。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of high status does not remember trivial matters. This is often used as a polite or flattering expression.

PROVERB: 贵人抬眼看，定是福星临
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指有地位高的人鼎力相助，好运肯定当头。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): With the strong support of a person of high standing, good fortune is sure to come your way.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指有身份的、地位高的人光临无身份的、地位低下者的住处。多用作迎宾语句。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of high status and distinction graces the humble dwelling of one of low position. This is often used as a welcoming expression for honored guests.

PROVERB: 锅里添水，不如釜底抽薪
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 釜：古时的炊事用具,类似于现在的锅。薪：柴火。想要不让水沸腾，用往锅里加水的手段，还不如撤走锅底下的柴火。比喻解决问题要从根本上下手。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Fǔ" is an ancient cooking vessel similar to a modern pot. "Xīn" means firewood. If you want to stop water from boiling, adding more water to the pot is less effective than removing the firewood beneath it. To solve a problem, one must address it at its root.

PROVERB: 国家多难之秋，壮士用命之时
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指国家多灾多难之时，有志之士应敢于为国家献身献策。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the nation faces multiple disasters and hardships, people of aspiration should dare to sacrifice themselves and offer their counsel for the country.

PROVERB: 国家将兴，必有祯祥；国家将亡，必有妖孽
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 祯祥：吉祥的征兆。妖孽：妖魔孽障，泛指怪异不祥的事物。国家将要兴旺发达，必定会有吉祥的征兆；国家将要衰败灭亡，必定会有怪异不祥的事情发生。比喻重大的事故出现之前都有特定的征兆。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Zhēnxiáng" means auspicious omens. "Yāoniè" means demons and calamities, broadly referring to strange and inauspicious phenomena. When a nation is about to prosper, there will surely be auspicious signs; when a nation is about to decline and fall, there will surely be strange and ominous events. Major catastrophes always have specific forewarnings before they occur.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是国家的兴旺衰败或灭亡，人人都有责任。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The rise, decline, or fall of a nation is every person's responsibility.

PROVERB: 国家有难思良将，人到中年望子孙
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指国家有了外患内乱便指望有良将出来平息；人到中年便盼望有子孙来传宗接代。古时的观念为无后是一大不孝。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When a nation faces external threats and internal disorder, it looks to capable generals to restore peace; when a man reaches middle age, he hopes for descendants to carry on the family line. In ancient thinking, having no heir was considered a great act of filial impiety.

PROVERB: 国将兴，听于民；国将亡，听于神
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指处处考虑到人民的意愿，国家就能兴旺发达；处处听从神灵摆布，国家就会衰败灭亡。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If a government considers the will of the people in all things, the nation will prosper; if it follows only the dictates of superstition and spirits, the nation will decline and perish.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 社稷：社,土神;稷：谷神。古代君王祭祀社稷，随后便以"社稷"措代国家。指国君有理由为国家而死。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Shèjì" — "shè" is the god of earth; "jì" is the god of grain. Ancient rulers offered sacrifices to these deities, and thus "shèjì" came to stand for the nation itself. A ruler has just cause to die for the sake of the nation.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 当国家遇到危难的时候，才能考验出哪个人是真正的忠臣。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only when the nation faces peril can one truly identify who is a loyal minister.

PROVERB: 国强民不受辱，民强国不受侮
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 只有国家强大了，人们才不会受到侮辱；人们能自强奋进，国家就可以避免受到欺侮。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only when the nation is strong will its people not be humiliated; when the people strive for self-improvement, the nation can avoid being bullied.

PROVERB: 国危思良将，世乱念忠臣
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指国家遇到危难、社会出现动乱的时候，迫切需要良将忠臣来平定动乱、治理国家。泛指在遇到困难之时，才意识到急需忠心耿耿能办事的忠臣。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the nation is in danger and society is in turmoil, there is an urgent need for capable generals and loyal ministers to quell the disorder and govern the country. In general, it is only when difficulties arise that one realizes how desperately loyal and capable servants are needed.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指国家不能有两个国君，就如天上不可以有两个太阳一样，要不然就会相互争斗，争权夺利，使天下大乱。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A nation cannot have two sovereigns, just as the sky cannot have two suns — otherwise there will be rivalry and power struggles, plunging the realm into chaos.

PROVERB: 国以民为本，民以食为天
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 对国家来讲，老百姓最重要；对老百姓来讲，吃饭最重要。意思是要关心老百姓的生活，尤其要关心老百姓的温饱问题。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): For the nation, the people are most important; for the people, food is most important. One must be concerned with the livelihood of the common people, especially the problem of ensuring they are fed and clothed.

PROVERB: 国以民为根，民以谷为命
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓国家的根本是老百姓，老百姓的命根子是粮食。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The foundation of a nation is its people; the lifeline of the people is grain.

PROVERB: 国有国法，官有官体，狱有狱例
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指一个国家，从上到下都必须有法律、规章或条例，用作规范人的行为，维护正常的社会秩序。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): From top to bottom, a nation must have laws, regulations, and statutes to govern people's behavior and maintain normal social order.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 一个国家有一个国家的法律，一个家庭有一个家庭的规矩。指不管任何事都要遵守相关的规章守则。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A nation has its laws; a family has its rules. In all matters, one must abide by the relevant regulations and codes.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指大到国家，小到家庭，都有管事的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): From the nation at the largest scale to the family at the smallest, there is always someone in charge.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 卒子：象棋中最小的一个子。意思是勇往苴前的小兵具有很强的战斗力。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Zúzi" is the smallest piece in Chinese chess. A foot soldier who charges forward bravely possesses formidable fighting power.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指只要指挥得力，普通的士兵也能威力无穷。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): As long as the command is effective, even ordinary soldiers can be invincible.

PROVERB: 过了这个村儿，没有这个店儿
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻错过了好机会，就不会再有这么好的机会了。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Once a good opportunity is missed, such a fine chance will not come again.

PROVERB: 海枯终见底，人死不知心
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 只有海水枯竭时，才能显露出海底。但一个人即便是死掉，也很难让他人了解到他生前心灵深处的故事。喻指人的心思难以揣测。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only when the sea dries up can its bottom be revealed. But even when a person dies, others can hardly know the deepest stories of their heart. The thoughts of a person are nearly impossible to fathom.

PROVERB: 海上风多舟难行，世上官多不太平
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 风多浪大，船只颠簸难行；官多扰民，百姓得不到安宁。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When winds are strong and waves are high, boats toss and cannot travel smoothly; when officials are too many and meddlesome, the common people find no peace.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指单从人的外表，不能估量他的身份和未来。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One cannot judge a person's identity or future merely from their outward appearance.

PROVERB: 寒门出将相，草莽出英雄
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时认为将帅、宰相之类的栋粱之才常常出身贫寒
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, it was believed that great generals and prime ministers — pillars of the state — often came from humble origins.

PROVERB: 寒门生贵子，白屋出公卿
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指穷苦人家往往出达官贵人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Illustrious officials and nobles often emerge from poor and lowly households.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 相传西汉时刘邦问他手下的将领韩信能带领多少军队打仗，韩信回答：多多益善。意思就是越多越好。
