EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Legend has it that in the Western Han dynasty, when Liu Bang asked his general Han Xin how many troops he could command, Han Xin answered: "The more the better." This means the more, the merrier.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是英雄豪杰对事物的见解基本上一致。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Heroes and outstanding minds tend to see things the same way.

PROVERB: 好的不在多，一个顶十个
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指入或物贵在品质精而不在数量多。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): What matters in people or things is quality, not quantity.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 经验丰富的人能对付各种困难的局面。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person rich in experience can handle all manner of difficult situations.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指好官容易做，好人却很难做。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): It is easy to be a good official, but hard to be a good person.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指有胆识的人，不轻举妄动，等候时机成熟再行动。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of true courage does not act rashly — they wait for the right moment before making their move.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指精明的人会见机行事，处于劣势逆境时，会暂作让步，避免吃亏受辱。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A shrewd person acts according to circumstances; when at a disadvantage or in adversity, they will temporarily yield to avoid suffering loss or humiliation.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指真正的好汉不向没有恶意或无力还手的人动武。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A true hero does not use force against those who mean no harm or who are unable to fight back.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓真正的好男儿能宽恕登门示好的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A true man of valor can forgive someone who comes to his door in a gesture of goodwill.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 有志气的男子不会欺负弱小者。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A man of ambition does not bully the weak and small.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指有作为的人会再接再厉，不在他人面前炫耀过去的成就。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of true accomplishment presses forward without boasting of past achievements before others.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指有志气的男子不怕自己出身卑微。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A man of ambition is not ashamed of humble origins.

PROVERB: 好汉不贪色，英雄不贪财
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指英雄好汉不受金钱美女的诱惑。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A true hero is not tempted by money or beauty.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指英雄好汉也得吃饱饭，谁也受不了连日饥饿。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even a hero must eat — no one can endure days of hunger.

PROVERB: 好汉护三村，好狗护三邻
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指英雄好汉理当保护和帮助邻里乡亲。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A hero should protect and help neighbors and fellow villagers.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 英雄好汉宁可自己流血牺牲，也不能掉眼泪祈求他人的同情。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A true hero would rather shed blood and sacrifice his life than shed tears begging for sympathy from others.

PROVERB: 好汉怕赖汉，赖汉还怕歪死缠
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 胡搅蛮缠不讲理的人比什么都不干的人还难于应付。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An unreasonable person who stirs up trouble is even harder to deal with than someone who does nothing at all.

PROVERB: 好汉怕赖汉，赖汉怕急汉
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 人被逼急了，什么事情都干得出来。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When a person is pushed to the breaking point, there is nothing they will not do.

PROVERB: 好汉识好汉，英雄识英雄
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指英雄好汉有识别英雄好汉的眼力
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A true hero has the eye to recognize another true hero.

PROVERB: 好汉天下有好汉，英雄背后有英雄
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指强人中间还有更强的人。劝诫人不要骄傲自满，忽视他人的力量。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Among the strong, there is always someone stronger. This cautions against arrogance and underestimating others.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指英雄好汉一言九鼎，说话算数，就像好马只要打一鞭子就能飞奔一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A true hero's word is his bond — what he says he will do, just as a fine horse needs only one crack of the whip to gallop.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指有志气的人会在功名事业上拼搏努力，只有庸碌的懒汉才会在衣食琐事上发生争执。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of ambition devotes their energy to fame and accomplishment; only the idle and mediocre quarrel over trivial matters of food and clothing.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指体魄健壮的男子也禁不住疾病的折磨。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even a robust and sturdy man cannot withstand the torment of illness.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 好汉子：此处指强者 有本事的人。乏：疲乏,困乏。意思是好汉不跟一时疲乏劳顿的敌手争高低。换句话说，强大者不欺负弱小者，有本事的人不同已经困乏的人争斗。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Hǎo hànzi" here refers to a strong and capable person. "Fá" means fatigued or exhausted. A true hero does not compete with an opponent who is temporarily weary and spent. In other words, the strong do not bully the weak, and the capable do not contend with those already exhausted.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指英雄好汉做事敢做敢当。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A true hero dares to do and dares to own what they have done.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 强壮的老虎也招架不住一群恶狼，形容寡不敌众。比喻一个人再强壮，有再大的本事，也招架不过众人的围攻。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even a powerful tiger cannot fend off a pack of wolves — this describes being outnumbered. No matter how strong or capable one person is, they cannot withstand the onslaught of many.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 好年盛景：丰收年。指在丰收的时候，到腊月时人们会欢闹喜庆。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Hǎo nián shèngjǐng" means a bountiful harvest year. In a year of good harvest, people celebrate joyously when the twelfth lunar month arrives.

PROVERB: 好拳不赢头三手，自有高招在后头
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指有本领的人不露锋芒，为自己留有余地，关键时刻才出绝招取胜。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A truly skilled person does not show off their edge, leaving room for themselves, and only reveals their decisive move at the critical moment.

PROVERB: 好手不敌双拳，双拳难敌四手
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 敌：抵挡。指有力的一只大手抵挡不住两个拳头，而两个拳头却敌不过四只大手有力。比喻少不胜多。也比喻即使一个人本领再高强，也会寡不敌众。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Dí" means to withstand. One powerful hand cannot fend off two fists, and two fists cannot overcome four powerful hands. The few cannot prevail against the many. No matter how formidable one person's skills, they will be outnumbered.

PROVERB: 好雁总是领头飞，好马总是先出列
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指有才能的人总是做领头羊，就如骏马总是跑在最前头一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A talented person always takes the lead, just as a fine horse always runs at the front of the pack.

PROVERB: 合群的喜鹊能擒鹿，齐心的蚂蚁能吃虎
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 用来比喻弱者齐心协力，也能战胜强者。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even the weak, when united in heart and effort, can defeat the strong.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 很难做到众人一心，团结一致。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): It is extremely difficult to achieve true unity of purpose among many people.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓做官的总存有私心，就好比是河流就必定会有鱼。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Those who serve as officials always harbor self-interest, just as any river will inevitably contain fish.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指人多了就会扯皮，相互推诿反而办不成事情。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When there are too many people involved, they will pass blame and shirk responsibility, making it impossible to get things done.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 钵盂：和尚用的饭具。比喻只要有人在，与他相关的东西也存茌。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Bōyú" is the bowl used by a Buddhist monk. As long as the person exists, the things associated with them will also be there.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指优秀的领头人对事业的成功起着至关重要的作用。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An outstanding leader plays a critically important role in the success of an undertaking.

PROVERB: 荷花虽好，也要绿叶扶持
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指人再有本领，也得需要有人扶助支持。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter how capable a person is, they still need the support and assistance of others.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时认为哄骗人不必承担法律责任。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, it was believed that deceiving people did not carry legal liability.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 侯门：指显贵人家。指显贵人家居住的传统住宅庭院深深，门禁森严，普通人很难进入。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Hóumén" refers to the households of the distinguished and noble. Their traditional residences have deep courtyards and strict gatekeeping, making it extremely difficult for ordinary people to gain entry.

PROVERB: 猴子不钻圈，多筛几遍锣
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 筛：此处指敲锣。比喻如果对方不上圈套，就需要多采用一些手段诱惑对方上圈套。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Shāi" here means to beat a gong. If the other party does not take the bait, one must employ additional tactics to lure them into the trap.

PROVERB: 狐狸再狡猾也斗不过好猎手
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻不论敌人如何狡猾，也斗不过智慧的人民群众。也比喻恶人再狡猾，其阴谋终究会被他人揭穿。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter how cunning the enemy, they cannot outwit the wisdom of the people. No matter how crafty an evildoer, their schemes will ultimately be exposed.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指人离开了自己的优势环境就不能充分地施展才华，就如同虎离开山、龙离开海一样失去了依靠的优势
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person who leaves their advantageous environment cannot fully display their talents, just as a tiger away from its mountain or a dragon away from the sea loses its source of strength.

PROVERB: 虎不与狮斗，兵不和匪争
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 不要同强悍的对手进行争斗。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Do not engage in a contest with a formidable adversary.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是把头伸进老虎嘴里。比喻自蹈险境。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Sticking one's head into a tiger's mouth — this means willingly walking into a deadly trap.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指恶人当道，好人就要遭殃。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When evil people hold power, good people will suffer.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指鲜花盛开时最担心大风的摧残。比喻好事怕出差错。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When flowers are in full bloom, what they fear most is the destruction of a gale. Good things are most vulnerable to going wrong.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 当事人不着急，局外人反而焦急万分。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The person directly involved is not anxious, yet the bystander is frantic with worry.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻畅销抢手的商品不用发愁卖不出去。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Goods that sell well and are in high demand need no worry about finding buyers.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 即使是地位显赫的贵人也会有贫贱卑微的亲戚。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even a person of the highest status and distinction has poor and humble relatives.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 老天辜负不了苦心人的意愿意指只要肯下苦工夫，坚持下去，愿望就一定会实现。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Heaven will not disappoint the wishes of those who toil with all their heart. As long as one is willing to work hard and persevere, one's wishes will surely be fulfilled.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指人才是无价之宝，比黄金更珍贵。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Talented people are a priceless treasure, more precious than gold.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指黄鼠狼专挑病鸭子咬。比喻坏人专找对方最脆弱的地方下手又比喻天灾人祸总是降临在弱小者的身上。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The weasel always picks the sick duck to bite. Evildoers always attack the most vulnerable point of their target, and disasters always befall the weak.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指灾荒年代，蝗虫肆意飞行，吃掉禾苗，不管地界。比喻古时有权势的人肆意侵吞、挥霍公款，不受法律制裁。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In years of famine, locusts fly rampantly, devouring crops without regard for boundaries. In ancient times, powerful people plundered and squandered public funds with impunity, beyond the reach of the law.

PROVERB: 浑浊不分鲢共鲤，水清方见两般鱼
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻社会腐败动荡，就容易混淆是非；国家政治清明，就会善恶分明。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When society is corrupt and turbulent, right and wrong are easily confused; when politics are clear and just, good and evil are plainly distinguished.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 混水好摸鱼。比喻混乱的局面有利于做坏事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Muddy water makes it easy to catch fish. A chaotic situation is favorable for doing bad deeds.

PROVERB: 火车跑得快，全靠车头带
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻精明的领导，可以带领人们迈向事业的成功。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A wise and capable leader can guide people toward the success of their endeavors.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 敌人是不服输的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An enemy will never willingly admit defeat.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 大家合伙打官司,各有各的想法，很难同心协力，不容易打赢。也泛指合伙办事，倾向于互相推诿，不容易成功。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When many people join together in a lawsuit, each has their own ideas, making it very hard to unite — and thus very hard to win. More broadly, when people collaborate on something, they tend to pass responsibility to each other, making success unlikely.

PROVERB: 鸡蛋碰不过石头，胳膊扭不过大腿
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻弱者无论怎样都打不过强者。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter what the weak do, they cannot defeat the strong.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 不可以无功受禄，不劳而食。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One must not accept rewards without merit or eat without working.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻两边都一无所获，空空如也
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Both sides end up with nothing — completely empty-handed.

PROVERB: 疾风知劲草，世乱识忠臣
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指在猛烈的大风下才能知道哪些是坚韧不拔的劲草，国家动乱之时，就能够识别出谁是真正的忠臣比喻在动乱的年代才能了解一个人忠心与否。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only under a fierce gale can one tell which grasses are tough and resilient; only in times of national turmoil can one identify who is truly loyal. It is only in turbulent times that one can know whether a person is truly faithful.

PROVERB: 既到灵山，岂可不朝我佛
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 灵山：印度的灵鹫山，相传释迦牟尼曾于此讲过经。到了灵山，就不得不朝拜佛祖。喻指到了一个新地方就一定得拜见主人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Língshān" refers to Vulture Peak in India, where it is said Shakyamuni once preached the sutras. Having arrived at Vulture Peak, one cannot help but pay respects to the Buddha. This means that when you arrive at a new place, you must pay your respects to the host.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 系：拴、缚。拴狗应当拴脖子。比喻攻打敌人要击中其要害之处。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Xì" means to tie or bind. When tying up a dog, one should tie it by the neck. When attacking an enemy, one must strike at the vital point.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指家法必须服从于国家大法。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Family rules must be subordinate to the laws of the state.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 不可能家里所有的人全部都参与犯罪。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): It is impossible that every single member of a household is involved in a crime.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 一户人家如果没有主妇，房屋也会倒转过来。喻指一个家庭，不能没有管理家务的主妇。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If a household has no mistress, the house itself would turn upside down. A family cannot do without a woman who manages domestic affairs.

PROVERB: 家有常业，虽饥不饿；国有常法，虽危不亡
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 一个家有正当固定的谋生手段在饥荒年代就不至于挨饿；国家有固定的法律，在危难之时就不会灭亡。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A family with a steady and legitimate livelihood will not go hungry even in years of famine; a nation with established laws will not perish even in times of crisis.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是说任何单位或团体，都必须有共同遵守的法规。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Any organization or group must have rules and regulations that all members observe together.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 不论哪个地方，都有主事负责的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter where you go, there is always someone in charge.

PROVERB: 家有诤子，不败其家；国有诤臣，不亡其国
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 无论家庭还是国家，只要有敢说实话的人，家庭就不会衰败，国家就不会灭亡。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Whether in a family or a nation, as long as there are people who dare to speak the truth, the family will not decline and the nation will not perish.

PROVERB: 家中百事兴，全靠主人命
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时认为主人的命运决定着家中的百事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, it was believed that the master's fate determined the fortunes of everything in the household.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 家中无鬼怪作祟，就可平安无事。常用来比喻国家如果没有叛逆奸贼，就不至于混乱衰亡。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If there are no ghosts or demons causing trouble within the home, all will be peaceful. This is often used as a metaphor: if a nation has no traitors or treacherous villains, it will not fall into chaos and decline.

PROVERB: 拣日不如撞日，撞日不如今日
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 刻意挑选日子不如碰日子，碰日子不如说干就干。劝诫大家不要迷信黄历。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Deliberately choosing an auspicious day is not as good as happening upon one, and happening upon one is not as good as acting right away. This urges people not to be superstitious about the almanac.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时百姓一旦被官吏传唤，常常凶多吉少，所以大家都害怕看见做官的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, once a commoner was summoned by an official, the outcome was usually dire — so everyone dreaded the sight of government officers.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指见害不除，等同犯罪。比喻见到坏人坏事不去制止就等同于有罪责。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): To see harm and not eliminate it is tantamount to committing a crime. To witness wrongdoing and not try to stop it is the same as bearing guilt oneself.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 橐驼：即骆驼。指看到骆驼不认识，却主观武断地认为是马肿背。比喻主观武断，对没有见过的东酉妄加猜说。讽刺见识浅薄、自作聪明的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Tuótuó" means camel. Seeing a camel for the first time and not recognizing it, one stubbornly assumes it is a horse with a swollen back. This mocks those who are narrow in experience and presumptuously guess about things they have never seen — people who are ignorant yet think themselves clever.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指夺取政权并不难，要得到人民群众的真心拥护却很难。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Seizing political power is not the hard part; winning the genuine support of the people is truly difficult.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 将领不激励士兵，士兵就不愿意奋勇作战。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If a general does not inspire and encourage the troops, the soldiers will not fight bravely.

PROVERB: 将军不下马，各自奔前程
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指各人走各人的路，谁也不干涉谁。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Each person walks their own path, and no one interferes with anyone else.

PROVERB: 将军额上跑下马，宰相肚里行舟船
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指将军和宰相的胸怀宽阔，气量很大，能容忍一切。常用来劝说人胸怀要宽广，气量要大。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The hearts of generals and chancellors are vast and magnanimous, able to tolerate all things. This is often used to urge people to be broad-minded and generous in spirit.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 将帅之家的后代肯定也勇敢。意指有才干或声望的家庭常有杰出的接班人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The descendants of a family of generals and marshals will surely be brave as well. Families of talent and renown often produce outstanding successors.

PROVERB: 将相本无种，男儿当自强
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 才干本领靠遗传是得不到的，男子汉应当奋发图强，自强不息。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Talent and ability cannot be obtained through heredity alone — a man should strive vigorously and ceaselessly improve himself.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指古时将相往往出身卑微。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, generals and chancellors often came from humble origins.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指有作为的将帅依靠谋略取胜，而不是仅借个人的勇敢。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A capable general relies on strategy to win, not merely on personal bravery.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时将军在外带兵打仗，有一定的主动权，可以不听从君主的命令。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, a general commanding troops far from the capital held a degree of autonomy and could choose not to obey certain orders from the sovereign.

PROVERB: 降龙自有降龙手，捉鬼还得捉鬼人
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指要降服何种对手，就得起用何种人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): To subdue a particular kind of opponent, one must employ the right kind of person for the task.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 再倔强的毛驴只要用鞭子狠狠抽打，也会驯服它。比喻固执倔强的人也惧怕强烈的打击。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even the most stubborn donkey can be tamed by a fierce whipping. Even the most obstinate person fears a powerful blow.

PROVERB: 浇花浇心儿，栽树栽根儿
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻解决问题要从根儿着手。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): To solve a problem, one must start from the root.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 骄傲轻敌的部队，肯定打不了胜仗。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An army that is arrogant and underestimates its enemy will certainly never win a battle.

PROVERB: 狡兔尽，猎狗烹；飞鸟尽，良弓藏；敌国破，良臣亡
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 野外的兔子没得逮了，猎犬就被煮吃；天上的飞鸟没得打了，弓箭就得收藏起来不能使用；敌国被消火了，功臣就被害死。多指帝王夺取政权以后，功臣良将常常被谋害或受到冷淡。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When all the wild rabbits have been caught, the hunting dogs are boiled and eaten; when all the birds in the sky have been shot down, the bows and arrows are put away; when the enemy state has been destroyed, the meritorious ministers are killed. This often refers to how, after an emperor seizes power, his loyal generals and meritorious officials are frequently murdered or cast aside.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 狡猾的兔子打很多洞，各洞之间相通连，以防不测。比喻有远见的人事先安排好避祸的打算。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A cunning rabbit digs many burrows, all interconnected, to guard against the unexpected. A person of foresight makes arrangements in advance to avoid disaster.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指叫唤的鸟儿只想着歌唱而忘了捕食。比喻往往因为爱闲谈笑话而误了正经事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A singing bird is so absorbed in its song that it forgets to hunt for food. People who are fond of idle chatter and jokes often neglect serious business.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 夏桀的狗朝贤君尧狂叫不止，是因为要向着自己的主人。指人各为自己的主人效力。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The dog of the tyrant Jie barks ceaselessly at the virtuous King Yao — not because Yao is bad, but because the dog is loyal to its own master. Everyone serves their own master.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 今后的事情不能预料。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Future events cannot be foreseen or predicted.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指忠孝不能两全。多用于奉劝人应以国事公务为重。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One cannot fulfill both loyalty to the state and filial piety to one's parents at the same time. This is often used to urge people to prioritize national affairs and public duties.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 在京城做官不如在外地做官，因为在外受制约少，容易搜到钱财。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Serving as an official in the capital is not as advantageous as serving in the provinces, because in the provinces one faces fewer constraints and finds it easier to accumulate wealth.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻白费力气，办事没有效率。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A metaphor for wasted effort and inefficient work.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指好言劝说不听从，只有强迫硬来才行得通。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Kind words of persuasion go unheeded; only coercion and force will get through.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指敬神要心诚意诚。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When worshipping the gods, one must do so with genuine sincerity of heart.

PROVERB: 九个月长虫吃耗子，三个月耗子吃长虫
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 长虫：蛇。耗子：老鼠。比喻有时候强者也害怕弱者。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Chángchóng" means snake. "Hàozi" means mouse. Sometimes even the strong fear the weak.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指见过大世面的人，不在乎小事。换句话说，见过大世面的人，不会将微小之事放在眼里。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person who has seen the world on a grand scale does not fuss over small matters. One who has experienced great things will not concern themselves with trifles.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指由于喝酒而引起的病，可以用酒来医治比喻因何物惹的灾祸，还得用何物来消除。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An illness caused by drinking can be cured with wine. A calamity caused by a certain thing must be resolved by that same thing.

PROVERB: 酒肉穿肠过，佛在心中坐
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 酒肉吃到肚子里，吃过便没有了，佛供奉在心里，永远伴着人。指敬佛重在心诚，不必恪守清规戒律。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Wine and meat go into the belly and are gone once consumed, but the Buddha enshrined in the heart accompanies a person forever. True devotion to the Buddha lies in sincerity of heart, not in rigid adherence to monastic rules and dietary restrictions.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是军事救助非常关紧，一刻也不能耽误。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Military relief is a matter of the utmost urgency — not a single moment can be wasted.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是害怕法律威严，不干坏事，就能安居乐业。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Those who fear the majesty of the law and refrain from wrongdoing can live and work in peace and contentment.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指疲倦的鸟也知道返回自己的窝巢。比喻长时间在外地生活、年事已高的人经常想要返回家乡，落叶归根。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even a weary bird knows to return to its own nest. A person who has lived far from home for many years and grown old often longs to return to their homeland — like fallen leaves returning to their roots.

PROVERB: 军不斩不齐，将不严不整
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指军中赏罚不明，将领治军不严，军队的作风就不会严谨。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When rewards and punishments in the military are unclear and the commander is lax in discipline, the army's conduct will not be rigorous.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指执行军事命令要如同高山突然倒下一般地迅速，不能有丝毫的马虎。比喻士兵必须绝对服从军令。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Military orders must be executed as swiftly as a mountain suddenly collapsing, with not the slightest room for carelessness. Soldiers must obey military commands absolutely.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 执行军令容不下私人感情。也指对于不遵守军令的士兵，不可以徇私情。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The execution of military orders leaves no room for personal feelings. Soldiers who disobey orders must not be shown favoritism.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指军令一出，就像山一样不可动摇，不管谁都必须服从。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Once a military order is issued, it is as immovable as a mountain — everyone, without exception, must obey.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 逾：超过。指军队中应该及时行赏，不宜拖延。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Yú" means to exceed or surpass. Rewards in the military should be given promptly and must not be delayed.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指军队中要是没了口粮必然不打自乱。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If an army runs out of provisions, it will inevitably fall into disorder without even being attacked.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 媒：媒介，指向导或内应。士兵去袭击敌方，若没有向导或内应，即使已经走到半路，也必须返回。又指军队前行时若没有向导指路，就到达不了目的地。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Méi" means a guide or an inside agent. When soldiers go to raid the enemy, if they have no guide or inside agent, they must turn back even if they are already halfway there. An army that marches without a guide cannot reach its destination.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指任何地方都有领头管事的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Every place has someone who takes the lead and manages affairs.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 军队若是没有了粮草，肯定会不攻自乱。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If an army loses its supply of grain and fodder, it will certainly collapse into chaos without any need for an attack.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指军队中开玩笑的话是没有的。比喻在某种环境下讲的话非常严肃而慎重。也比喻在军队里，军纪严明，讲话一定得严肃认真，不可以随意说玩笑话。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): There is no such thing as a joke in the military. In certain settings, words are spoken with the utmost gravity and seriousness. In the army, discipline is strict, speech must be serious, and casual jokes are not permitted.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指有谋略的人等待合适的时机才进行报复。换句话说，报仇雪恨的大事不可操之过急，必须把握有利时机，才能取得成功。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of strategic mind waits for the right moment to take revenge. The great matter of vengeance must not be rushed — one must seize the opportune moment to succeed.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指品格高尚的人不与性格粗鲁的人发生争斗。也指有修养的人不跟无知的人计较。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of noble character does not quarrel with someone who is coarse and rude. A person of refinement does not stoop to bickering with the ignorant.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指有修养的人讲究的是礼貌，品德不高的人则喜欢争斗。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of cultivation values courtesy and propriety; a person of low moral character is fond of quarreling and fighting.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是大丈夫一句话，分量很重。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The word of a true man carries immense weight.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 大丈夫一言既出，就如同着鞭的快马一样，不可以收回来。意指言而有信。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Once a true man has given his word, it is like a swift horse that has felt the whip — it cannot be taken back. One must be true to one's word.

PROVERB: 君不正臣不忠，父不正子不孝
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 国君不公正臣就会不尽忠，父亲不正派儿子也不会孝顺。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If the sovereign is not fair, the ministers will not be loyal; if the father is not upright, the son will not be filial.

PROVERB: 君不正臣投外国，父不正子奔他乡
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 国君无道，做臣子的就会投靠别国；父行邪恶，儿子就会离家出走。指上行不正,下面就会采用叛离的行为。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If the sovereign is unjust, the ministers will defect to another state; if the father practices evil, the son will leave home. When those above set a crooked example, those below will respond with betrayal and desertion.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时指君主与臣子的关系好比父与子的关系。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, the relationship between sovereign and minister was likened to that between father and son.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 君王说话一定得算话，不可以随意乱说。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A sovereign's words must always be kept — they must not be spoken carelessly or recklessly.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 弓拉开却不射箭。意指假装出强大的声威和气势。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Drawing the bow but not releasing the arrow — this means putting on a show of great power and momentum without actually striking.

PROVERB: 砍不倒大树，弄不多柴火
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 砍大树固然费力气,但是能获得更多的柴火。意思是只有征服了强大的对手才会有很多收获。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Felling a large tree is certainly laborious, but it yields far more firewood. Only by conquering a formidable opponent can one reap great rewards.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻征服比自己强大的对手有非常多的收益。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Defeating an opponent stronger than oneself brings extraordinarily abundant gains.

PROVERB: 看风使舵常顺利，随机应变信如神
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 根据客观情况的发展变化，适时调整自己的对策和行动，才能顺利办事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One must adjust one's strategies and actions in a timely manner according to the development and changes of objective circumstances in order to accomplish things smoothly.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指看人要看这个人心肠的好坏，听话要留心言外之意。换句话说，判断一个人要看他的内心表现怎么样，听话则应听出他的真正意图来。说明观察事物要仔细，要透过现象看到本质。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When judging a person, look at whether their heart is good or bad; when listening to words, pay attention to the meaning behind them. In other words, to assess a person, examine their inner character; to understand speech, discern the speaker's true intent. One must observe things carefully and see through appearances to the essence.

PROVERB: 靠着大河有水吃，靠着大树有柴烧
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指依靠有权势的人，就可以得到相关的利益。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): By relying on someone with power and influence, one can obtain corresponding benefits.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指长在树下的草，风霜侵不到比喻有权势者的庇护，没有人敢侵犯。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Grass growing beneath a great tree is sheltered from wind and frost. Under the protection of a powerful person, no one dares to cause harm.

PROVERB: 慷慨成仁易，从容就义难
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 为正义事业意气昂扬地奉献出自己的生命可以做到，但要从容不迫地去死却办不到。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One can march courageously to lay down one's life for a righteous cause, but to face death with calm composure is far more difficult.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思指培养、包庇和纵容恶人，将祸患无尽
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): To nurture, harbor, and indulge evildoers is to breed endless calamity.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 苛政：严苛的政令。指严苛的政令会伤害老百姓，最终导致失去民心。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Kēzhèng" means harsh and oppressive governance. Tyrannical policies harm the common people and ultimately lead to the loss of the people's hearts.

PROVERB: 肯在热灶里烧火，不肯在冷灶里添柴
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 乐意攀附权贵，不愿帮助处在贫困中的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Eager to attach oneself to the rich and powerful, unwilling to help those in poverty and hardship.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 原是佛教用语。苦海，指深重的苦难。岸，指彼岸。佛教把得到正果称作到达彼岸。比喻虽罪孽深重，但只要弃恶从善，就会有出路。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Originally a Buddhist term. "Kǔhǎi" means a sea of profound suffering. "Àn" means the other shore. In Buddhism, attaining enlightenment is described as reaching the other shore. No matter how deep one's sins, as long as one renounces evil and embraces good, there is a way out.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓暂时处于困境而有抱负的人终于可以有出头之日。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person of ambition who is temporarily mired in hardship will eventually have the chance to rise and succeed.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指不能自己伤害自己。换句话说，自己人不会伤害自己人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One must not harm oneself. In other words, one's own people will not hurt their own.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻攀附权贵。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A metaphor for clinging to and currying favor with the powerful and influential.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指轻率地对待强者。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Refers to treating a strong opponent rashly and carelessly.

PROVERB: 腊月二十三，家家糖瓜粘
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 糖瓜：用麦芽糖做成的瓜状甜食。腊月二十三日，用糖果点心作为祭品。灶神吃后，嘴上粘糖，上天会讲好话。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Tángguā" (sugar melon) is a melon-shaped sweet made from maltose. On the 23rd of the twelfth lunar month, candy and pastries are offered as sacrifices to the Kitchen God. After eating them, his lips become sticky with sugar, so when he ascends to heaven he will only speak sweet words.

PROVERB: 腊月二十三，灶爷上了天，先生放了学，学生出了监
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时民风，腊月二十三这天是灶王爷上天的日子，学校在这一天开始放寒假，老师和学生都回家过年。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): According to ancient folk custom, the 23rd of the twelfth lunar month is the day the Kitchen God ascends to heaven. On this day, schools would begin winter vacation, and teachers and students all returned home for the New Year.

PROVERB: 腊月二十五，掸房扫尘土
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指在腊月二十五这一天，每家都打扫卫生准备迎接新春佳节。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): On the 25th of the twelfth lunar month, every household sweeps and cleans in preparation for the New Year festival.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 敢来的人是不会惧怕的，不好惹的。比喻不能轻视敢于前来挑战的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Those who dare to come are not afraid and are not to be trifled with. One should never underestimate those who dare come forward to issue a challenge.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指不厉害的不可能来，来的肯定是相当厉害的。喻指来的人不怀好意。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Those who are not formidable would not bother coming; those who come are certainly formidable. The visitors harbor ill intentions.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻不成器的人，再怎么扶持也不管用。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A metaphor for someone who will never amount to anything — no amount of support or assistance will make any difference.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻没有出息的人，依靠别人无论如何也扶持不起来。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person without ambition cannot be propped up no matter how much others try to help.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻能力再低下的人也总会能起上一点作用的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even a person of the lowest ability can still serve some purpose.

PROVERB: 浪再大，压不住鱼打挺；云再厚，裹不住炸雷声
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指对方势力再强大也难不住本领高强的人。也比喻任何力量都拦不住真理的传播。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter how powerful the opposing force, it cannot stop a person of extraordinary skill. Likewise, no force can halt the spread of truth.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 浪荡子改过后比黄金还值钱。意指犯过错误的人真正悔改之后不会再犯。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A prodigal son who truly reforms is worth more than gold. One who genuinely repents of past errors will not repeat them.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 老巢：鸟的老窝，比喻人的老家。指人不愿远离自己的老家。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Old nest" — a bird's old roost, used as a metaphor for one's hometown. People are reluctant to stray far from their native place.

PROVERB: 老龟煮不烂，移祸于枯桑
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 相传三国时有人献大龟给孙权，孙权让人煮龟，用了上万车柴仍然煮不烂。诸葛亮建议用老桑树煮，很快就煮烂了。意指嫁祸于人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Legend holds that during the Three Kingdoms period, someone presented a great turtle to Sun Quan. He ordered it cooked, but tens of thousands of cartloads of firewood could not cook it through. Zhuge Liang suggested using old mulberry wood, and it was quickly done. This means to shift blame onto another person.

PROVERB: 老虎不在家，猴子称大王
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻首领不在的时候，下属就有可能称王称霸。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the leader is absent, subordinates may seize the chance to lord it over others.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 坏人即使不做坏事，坏名声也巳经传开了。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even if a bad person refrains from doing evil, their bad reputation has already spread far and wide.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指事情比较复杂，不知道该从何处下手去解决。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The matter is so complex that one does not know where to begin solving it.

PROVERB: 老虎花在背，人心花在内
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 老虎的花纹长在皮毛上，人的主意谋划藏在内心里。意指人心难测。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A tiger's stripes are on its hide, but a person's schemes are hidden deep within the heart. The human heart is unfathomable.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻只要东西有用处，就不要嫌弃，不能丢弃。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): As long as something is useful, one should not despise it or cast it away.

PROVERB: 老虎还有个打盹儿的时候
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指再精明强悍的入也难免有不留神出差错的时候。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even the shrewdest and most formidable person will inevitably have moments of carelessness and error.

PROVERB: 老虎金钱豹，各走各的道
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 每个人有每个人的前程，各走各的路，互不干涉。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Everyone has their own future; each walks their own road without interfering with others.

PROVERB: 老虎口中夺脆骨，蛟龙背上揭生鳞
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是冒险行事，成功的希望很渺茫。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Taking risks with very little hope of success.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思指自以为很了不起，不愿意听取别人的批评。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Thinking oneself great and refusing to listen to others' criticism.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指触犯强横霸道的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Refers to provoking tyrannical and domineering people.

PROVERB: 老虎嘴里掉不下肉，狐狸嘴里吐不出鸡
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻坏人抢劫去的东西很难再要回来，也比喻坏人的本性不容易改掉。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Things seized by villains are nearly impossible to recover; likewise, a villain's nature is nearly impossible to change.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 泛指老手经验丰富，一人能顶几个人用。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): An experienced hand is so skilled that one person alone can do the work of several.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻经验丰富的人可以起到引导性的作用。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person rich in experience can serve a guiding role for others.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指人的本性难改。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person's fundamental nature is extremely difficult to change.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指坏人坏事处处都遭到大家的厌弃和打击。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Bad people and bad deeds are universally despised and attacked wherever they appear.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指人急了就会做出反常的事情来。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When pushed to extremes, people will do things completely out of character.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓目光短浅，没有远见。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Short-sighted and lacking in foresight.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 经常用来比喻坏人不在自己的住所附近做坏事而是到远方去犯罪。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Often used to describe how villains do not commit crimes near their own homes but travel far away to offend.

PROVERB: 老子偷瓜盗果，儿子杀人放火
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓如果做父亲的偷偷摸摸窃贼，儿子就有可能明火执仗当强盗。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If the father is a petty sneak-thief, the son may well become an outright armed robber.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 父亲如果是英雄人物，儿子也定不会差。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If the father is a hero, the son will surely not be far behind.

PROVERB: 冷眼观螃蟹，横行到几时
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 螃蟹：喻指恶人。意谓横行霸道的恶人不会有好下场，总有一天会遭到报应的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Crab" is a metaphor for a tyrant. Those who act like tyrants will not come to a good end; sooner or later retribution will find them.

PROVERB: 离家三里远，别是一乡风
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 风：风俗。指即使离家乡很近的地区，风俗习惯也与家乡不一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Fēng" means customs. Even places very close to one's hometown may have quite different customs and habits.

PROVERB: 离了胡萝卜，照样办酒席
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻没有某些无关紧要的人，工作照常开展。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without certain unimportant individuals, work carries on just the same.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 平定乱世容易，治理太平盛世却不容易。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Quelling a chaotic era is easy; governing well in times of peace and prosperity is far more difficult.

PROVERB: 立法不可不严，行法不可不恕
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时指制定法律要从严，执行法律要从宽。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times it was said that laws should be drafted strictly but enforced leniently.

PROVERB: 利不百，不变法；功不十，不易器
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 利益达不到百倍，法令不变更；功效不足十倍，工具不改换。古时抵制变革的一种借口。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If the benefit is not a hundredfold, do not change the decree; if the improvement is not tenfold, do not replace the tool. This was an ancient excuse for resisting reform and change.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指操练士兵首先要做好士兵的思想工作。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Training soldiers must begin with winning their hearts and minds.

PROVERB: 良禽择木而栖，贤臣择主而事
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时认为贤能的臣子要择取明主效力，就如同好鸟要择取好的树木柄息一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times it was held that a worthy minister should choose a wise sovereign to serve, just as a good bird chooses a fine tree on which to roost.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指粮草供应与战争的胜败关系重大。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The supply of provisions and fodder is critically related to victory or defeat in war.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指粮草给养充足，士气才能高涨。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only when grain and supplies are plentiful can the morale of the troops run high.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是交战中的双方，都不可以将对方派来的使者斩首。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Neither side in a conflict may execute the other side's envoy.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指两军交战，英勇作战的一方必然胜利。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When two armies clash, the side that fights with greater courage will certainly prevail.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻强手与强手相争，必定有一方会受伤失败。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When two powerful opponents contend, one will inevitably be injured and defeated.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指两强在一起肯定要争斗，不可能两者同时并存。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Two powerful forces cannot coexist in the same place; they are bound to clash.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 枪：古时的一种兵器。快要上阵了才匆忙磨枪头，虽然不锋利，但也可以光亮一点。比喻平常不做谁备，遇到急事急忙应付。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Qiāng" is an ancient weapon. Sharpening one's spear only at the last moment before battle — though not truly sharp, at least it gleams a little. This describes someone who normally makes no preparations and scrambles to cope only when urgency strikes.

PROVERB: 令出山摇动，法严鬼神惊
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 政治军令下达连山都震摇，法令严明连鬼神都震惊。指军令国法人人都必须服从。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When political and military orders are issued, even mountains shake; when laws are stern, even ghosts and spirits tremble. Military orders and national laws must be obeyed by everyone without exception.

PROVERB: 六月六，家中猫犬水中浴
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时风俗，农历六月初六给猫狗洗浴以避免生虫虱。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): According to ancient custom, on the 6th day of the 6th lunar month, cats and dogs were bathed to prevent lice and parasites.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指不能离开自己的权位或势力范围龙多旱，人多乱龙多了下不了雨，人多了会生乱。比喻人多了，做事情相互推诿，不尽职责，办事就没有效率。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One must not leave one's position of authority or sphere of influence. Too many dragons cause drought; too many people cause disorder. When there are too many people in charge, everyone shirks responsibility and nothing gets done efficiently.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻人太多或者太少，都做不好事情。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Too many people or too few people — either extreme hinders getting things done well.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指各自回到可以展示自己才华的地方去。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Each person returns to the place where they can best display their talents.

PROVERB: 龙生龙，凤生凤，老鼠养儿会打洞
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓子女的秉性特点是由父母那里遗传来的，上一代什么样就会培养出什么样的下一代。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Children's temperaments and traits are inherited from their parents; whatever the older generation is like, so too will the younger generation turn out.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻有什么样的父母，就会教养出什么样后代。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Whatever the parents are like, such will be the children they raise.

PROVERB: 龙无头不走，鸟无头不飞
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 龙没有头没法行走，鸟没有头没法飞翔。意谓不论做什么事情，都要有个带头的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A dragon cannot move without its head; a bird cannot fly without its head. No matter the undertaking, there must always be someone to take the lead.

PROVERB: 龙眼识珠，凤眼识宝，牛眼识青草
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 有眼力的人才能识别出优劣。换句话说，有眼光有水平的人见识就高，没眼光没水平的人见识就不高。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only those with discerning eyes can distinguish the superior from the inferior. People of insight and ability see farther; those without see less.

PROVERB: 龙游浅水遭虾戏，虎落平原被犬欺
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 龙游到浅水中会遭遇虾的戏弄老虎流落到平地上就会被狗欺侮。意指离开了必要条件，强者就会受制于弱者。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A dragon stranded in shallow water is mocked by shrimp; a tiger fallen to the flatlands is bullied by dogs. Removed from the conditions they need, the strong become subject to the weak.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指两强相互争斗，受害的是弱小的笫三者。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When two powerful forces battle each other, it is the weak third party that suffers most.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻若防范不严谨，有漏洞，恶人就会乘虚而人，做坏事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If defenses are lax and there are loopholes, evildoers will exploit the gaps to do harm.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指如果防范不严密，坏人就会钻空子。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If precautions are not strict, bad people will find openings to exploit.

PROVERB: 篱笆扎得紧，野狗钻不进
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指如果自己内部防范严密，坏人就没有机会可乘。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If one's own internal defenses are tight, bad people will have no opportunity to take advantage.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 篱笆扎牢了，野狗就不会钻进去。比喻只要防备严密，坏人就没有钻空子的机会。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the fence is firmly built, stray dogs cannot squeeze through. As long as defenses are tight, villains have no gaps to exploit.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 拿到手的锋利兵器不可以转借给他人。意谓手中掌握的权力不可以转让给他人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A sharp weapon in hand must not be lent to another. Power that one holds must not be transferred to others.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓人们总是会干方百计地到有利可图的地方去。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): People will always find ways, by hook or by crook, to go wherever there is profit to be had.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指夹在婆婆和姑娘之间的媳妇最不好当。泛指夹在两个地位高的人之间左右为难，上下不是。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The daughter-in-law caught between her mother-in-law and her own daughter is in the hardest position of all. More broadly, being stuck between two superiors and unable to please either is an extremely awkward predicament.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 薮：指人或物聚集的地方。指利益汇集、优厚的地方，往往就是人们怨尤集中的地方。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Sǒu" means a place where people or things gather. Wherever benefits are concentrated and generous, that is also where grievances and resentments tend to converge.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指只有在烈火的锻炼中才能得到真正的黄金。比喻通过严峻的考验才可以发现品质优秀的人或意志坚强的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only through the tempering of fierce flames can true gold be obtained. Only through severe trials can people of excellent character or unyielding will be discovered.

PROVERB: 临崖勒马收缰晚，船到江心补漏迟
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 临：到。指已经走到悬崖边才记起停马收缰，就已经晚了。船已行使到江中央才想起补漏洞，就来不及了。比喻要及早发现问题，抓紧时间采取补救措施。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Lín" means to arrive at. Remembering to rein in one's horse only at the edge of a cliff is already too late; thinking to patch a leak when the boat is already in mid-river is too late. One must discover problems early and take remedial action without delay.

PROVERB: 留情不举手，举手不留情
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 动手就表明彼此之间的情面没法讲了。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Coming to blows means that all pretense of courtesy between the parties has been abandoned.

PROVERB: 留下斗和秤，为的是公平
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指古人留传下的斗和秤，目的是要人们公平办事，不徇私情。比喻处事应当公平。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The measures and scales passed down from the ancients were intended to ensure that people deal with one another fairly and impartially. One should handle affairs with fairness.

PROVERB: 柳树上着刀，桑树上出血
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指代人受过。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Refers to taking the blame or punishment in someone else's place.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指高贵的人一旦没有权势，其身价连平常人都比不上。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Once a person of high station loses power, their worth falls below even that of an ordinary commoner.

PROVERB: 落他矮檐下，怎敢不低头
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 在低矮的屋檐下，只能低头走路。意指受制于他人的管束，就得忍气吞声。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Under low eaves, one can only walk with bowed head. When under another's control, one must swallow one's pride and endure in silence.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻四处钻空子谋利。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A metaphor for exploiting loopholes everywhere in pursuit of profit.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 六耳：一人有两耳，三人为六耳。指不能与很多人一起策划机密事，否则会泄漏机密。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Six ears": one person has two ears, so three people have six ears. Confidential plans must not be discussed among too many people, or the secret will be leaked.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是见义勇为的人，遇上不公平的事，敢于主持正义，帮助受欺负的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A person who acts bravely for justice, upon encountering unfairness, dares to stand up for what is right and help those who are being oppressed.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指道路可能有几干条，但真理却只有一个。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): There may be thousands of roads, but truth is only one.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指露水碰见太阳就消失了。比喻恶人不可能长时间存在。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Dew vanishes the moment it meets the sun. Evil people cannot endure for long.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指可做选择的太多，致使人不好拿定主意。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When there are too many choices, it becomes difficult to make up one's mind.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 混乱时代常能造就出英雄人物。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Times of chaos and turmoil often give rise to heroic figures.

PROVERB: 乱世出英雄，阵前识好汉
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 乱世才能显示出英雄是谁，战场上才能识别好汉是谁。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Only in turbulent times can true heroes be revealed; only on the battlefield can genuine warriors be identified.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指动乱年代流言蜚语也最多。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In times of upheaval, rumors and slander are at their most abundant.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓动乱年代可以考验一个人是否忠诚。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Turbulent times serve to test whether a person is truly loyal.

PROVERB: 乱世群雄起，有枪便为王
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 在战乱的年代，只要掌握武装力量就能称王称霸。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In an era of war and chaos, whoever commands armed force can dominate and rule.

PROVERB: 萝卜拔了窝窝在，和尚走了庙子在
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指人逃脱了，但家却搬不走。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The person may escape, but the home cannot be moved away.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 把马放归山里，武器放进仓库。意谓天下太平，没有战事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Releasing the horses into the mountains and storing the weapons in the armory — the world is at peace and there is no more war.

PROVERB: 马骑上等马，牛用中等牛，人使下等人
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 上等马：指跑得快的好马。中等牛：指温顺的牛。下等人：指不英明的人。古时富贵人家以为，骑马要骑上等良马，可以跑得快跑得远；用牛要用中等性情的牛，稳妥；使唤人要使唤那些不精明的人，才容易控制这说明了封建礼教的愚民思想。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Top-grade horse" means a fast, excellent steed. "Middle-grade ox" means a docile, steady ox. "Low-grade person" means an unwise servant. In ancient times, wealthy families believed one should ride the finest horse for speed and distance, employ a middling ox for its steadiness, and use unclever servants because they are easier to control. This reflects the feudal ideology of keeping common people ignorant and compliant.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指地位卑微的人凭借官府的权力耀武扬威。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Refers to a person of lowly status who flaunts power and bullies others by relying on the authority of officialdom.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指宁可多吃亏，也愿意求得平安无事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One would rather suffer repeated losses than forfeit peace and safety.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 真相不让上级了解，对下级却无所顾忌。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The truth is concealed from superiors while subordinates are treated without any restraint.

PROVERB: 满城文运转，遍地是方巾
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 文运：本指文学盛衰的气运，此处指官运。方巾：明代读书人常戴的方形软帽。指一人侥幸科第，宗族姻亲并换儒巾。古时讥讽时弊之语。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Wényùn" originally referred to the fortunes of literary achievement but here means official career fortune. "Fāngjīn" is the square soft cap commonly worn by Ming dynasty scholars. When one person is lucky enough to pass the imperial examinations, the entire clan and in-laws all change their caps in reflected glory. This was an ancient satirical quip about social ills.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻管事的人离开了，下属就会胡来。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the person in charge leaves, subordinates will act recklessly and do as they please.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 没有了屠户，就得吃带毛的猪肉。比喻如果没有内行知情的人，事情就不好办。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without a butcher, one would have to eat pork with the hair still on. Without a knowledgeable expert, things simply cannot be done properly.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指没有水就不能控制或扑灭火。喻指没有钱就不能解决困难。也比喻如果没有合适的措施，就解染不了实际问题。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without water, fire cannot be controlled or extinguished. Without money, difficulties cannot be resolved. Without appropriate measures, real problems cannot be solved.

PROVERB: 没有打虎将，过不得景阳冈
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 没有敢于奋勇拼搏的人，就熬不过难关。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without people who dare to fight courageously, one cannot endure through a crisis.

PROVERB: 没有带头羊，羊群难过河；没有带头骡，马帮难得驮
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻做事情必须有一个精明的领头人，否则不可能成功。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): To accomplish anything, there must be a shrewd and capable leader; otherwise success is impossible.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻没有优秀的人才，只好先用稍差一点的人来凑合。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Without excellent talent available, one must make do with slightly lesser people to fill the gap.

PROVERB: 没有闪电，雷不会响；没有刮风，树不会摇
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻事情的发生，总有相应的原因。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Every event that occurs has a corresponding cause behind it.

PROVERB: 没有三板斧，上不了瓦岗寨
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 三板斧：瓦岗军将领程咬金的绝招。瓦岗寨：隋末翟让领导的农民起义军，以瓦岗寨【今河南滑县】为根据地。比喻如果没有克敌制胜的武器，难关就攻不破。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Three axe blows" was the signature technique of Cheng Yaojin, a general of the Wagang army. The Wagang Stronghold was the base of the peasant uprising led by Zhai Rang at the end of the Sui dynasty, located in what is now Hua County, Henan. Without a decisive weapon to overcome the enemy, one cannot break through a difficult pass.

PROVERB: 门前结起高头马，不是亲来也是亲
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指人一旦有了势力，与自己没有亲属关系的人也都来攀附。也用于指奉承依附有权势的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Once a person gains power and influence, even those with no family connection will come flocking to attach themselves. Also used to describe those who flatter and cling to the powerful.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 门神：旧俗指贴在门上用来驱邪逐鬼的神像。一边是秦叔宝的画像，一边是尉迟恭的画像。比喻人上年纪了，体力衰退，反应不灵敏，办不成大事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Door gods: in old custom, images posted on doors to ward off evil spirits — one side bearing the portrait of Qin Shubao, the other that of Yuchi Gong. This is used as a metaphor for someone who is old and declining in physical strength, slow in reflexes, and no longer capable of great deeds.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 勇猛的将军手中如果没有武器也杀不了敌人。意谓没有必要的条件，本事再大也不行。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even a brave general cannot slay enemies if he has no weapon in his hands. Without the necessary conditions, no amount of ability will suffice.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时在庙里常常用猪头作祭品供神或供祖先。常用来喻指女子已经有了婆家。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, pig heads were commonly used as sacrificial offerings to gods or ancestors in temples. This is often used figuratively to indicate that a woman already has a fiancé or husband.

PROVERB: 妙药难医冤债病，横财不富命
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 穷人冤债病：冤鬼、债鬼纠缠的病。横财：用不正当手段谋取的钱财。指灵丹妙药治不了冤鬼、债鬼纠缠的病，不义之财不能使命中注定贫穷的人富裕起来。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Diseases caused by avenging ghosts and debt-spirits" cannot be cured by any miracle drug; ill-gotten wealth cannot make a person destined for poverty become rich.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 老百姓不检举揭发，官府就不会追究过问。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If the common people do not report and expose wrongdoing, the authorities will not investigate or pursue it.

PROVERB: 民乱则国破，国破则君主亡
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 老百姓乱套了，国家就会灭亡，君主就无法生存。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When the common people fall into chaos, the nation will perish and the sovereign cannot survive.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 民众是国家的立根之本。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The people are the very foundation upon which a nation stands.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 民众的意愿是不能轻视忽略的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The will of the people must never be taken lightly or ignored.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指失去民心就像水源干涸，树根千枯一样，必然会灭亡。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Losing the people's hearts is like water drying up at its source or a tree's roots withering — destruction inevitably follows.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 抱拳：一种礼节。比喻当面谦恭，却在背后攻击的两面派手法。换句话说,对那些当面很讲礼节，背厉作恶的伪善者，要小心提防。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Clasping fists" is a gesture of courtesy. This describes the two-faced tactic of being deferential to someone's face while attacking them from behind. One must be wary of hypocrites who are exceedingly polite in your presence but commit evil behind your back.

PROVERB: 明镜可以照形，古事可以知今
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 历史是现今的镜子，应以历史为鉴。换句话说，明亮的镜子可以用做照形体，借鉴古代的事情可以用来认识现今。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): History is a mirror for the present; one should take history as a lesson. A bright mirror can be used to examine one's appearance; studying ancient events can illuminate the present.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指公开的袭击容易对付，暗地里的算计不好防备。也指明面公开的攻击好应付，暗中潜藏的偷袭难于防备。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Open attacks are easy to handle; covert schemes are difficult to guard against. A frontal assault can be parried, but a hidden ambush is hard to foresee and prevent.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指称赞光明磊落的人就说明语，隐匿难懂的话不说。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Praising those who are open and upright means speaking plainly and clearly, without resorting to obscure or hidden language.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指赞誉光明磊落的人，见不得人的话不说，见不得人的事不做。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One should praise the straightforward and honorable: do not say what cannot be said openly, and do not do what cannot be done openly.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指对于做坏事的人，明地里有国家王法，暗地里有神灵问罪。告诫人们不要胡作非为，胡乱来。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): For those who do evil: in the open, there is the law of the land to deal with them; in secret, there are divine spirits to pass judgment. This warns people not to act recklessly or lawlessly.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指明处用掉，丢失了，暗中又可以得到。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): What is spent or lost openly may be recovered through hidden channels.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 魔：梵语"魔罗"的简称，指破坏修行的恶魔，比如"烦恼、迷恋"等，也指邪气。道：道行,佛家修行的功夫，也指正气。原是佛教用语，告诫修行的人要警惕世俗的迷惑。后用来比喻正义力量总能战胜邪恶的势力。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Mó" is abbreviated from the Sanskrit "Māra," referring to demons that obstruct spiritual cultivation — such as vexation, attachment, and other temptations — and more broadly to evil forces. "Dào" refers to the depth of one's spiritual practice and, by extension, to righteous force. Originally a Buddhist term cautioning practitioners against the seductions of the mundane world, it later came to express the idea that justice ultimately triumphs over evil.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 树梢过重，树干必折；尾巴过大，意指部属势力过大，就不容易控制，产生威胁。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When branches grow too heavy, the trunk will snap; when the tail grows too large, it cannot be wagged. When subordinates amass too much power, they become difficult to control and pose a threat.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 谋取官位时如老鼠一样谨慎，取得官位时却如老虎一样凶悍。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): As cautious as a mouse when scheming to obtain office, but as fierce as a tiger once power is secured.

PROVERB: 木偶不会自己跳，背后定有牵线人
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指木偶会跳动，可以生动有神是因为幕后有人牵线操作。比喻某些人做坏事是因为背后有人指使操纵。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A puppet dances with lifelike animation because someone behind the curtain pulls the strings. Certain people commit evil because someone behind the scenes is directing and manipulating them.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 罅：缝隙。意思是树木腐朽了，就容易生长蛀虫；墙壁有了裂缝，蚂蚁就可以乘隙而入。比喻内乱容易招来外患。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Xià" means crack or crevice. When wood rots, it readily breeds boring worms; when walls develop cracks, ants can enter through the gaps. Internal decay easily invites external threats.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 抓贼时要抓住赃证，捉奸时要抓住男女双方。指查处违法者要重证据。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When catching a thief, one must seize the stolen goods as evidence; when catching adulterers, one must catch both parties together. Investigating lawbreakers requires solid evidence.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 男女一旦到了婚嫁年龄就应该结婚成家。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Once a man and woman reach marriageable age, they should marry and establish a household.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 南方水多，大家就擅长驾船；北方陆地多，大家就擅长骑马。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In the south where water is plentiful, people become skilled at boating; in the north where land dominates, people become skilled at horsemanship.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指每个地方的人长期养成的对食品味道的喜好不一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): People in different regions develop different long-standing preferences for the flavors of food.

PROVERB: 你有长箩索，人家有弯扁担
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指别人的对策可能会更高明。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The other party's counterstrategy may prove even more brilliant than one's own.

PROVERB: 你有你的关门计，我有我的跳墙法
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指能针对不同的情况，采取具体的计策对应。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Refers to the ability to adopt specific tactics suited to different situations.

PROVERB: 你有你的佛法，我有我的道行
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指各自都有各自的技能和本领，谁也不能制服了谁。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Each has their own skills and abilities; neither can subdue the other.

PROVERB: 你有千条妙计，我有一定之规
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓不论你说什么，我还是按我自己的原则做事
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter what you say, I will still act according to my own principles.

PROVERB: 鸟随鸾凤飞能远，人伴贤良品自高
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 鸾凤：传说中凤凰一类的鸟。指普通的鸟追随着鸾凤，也可以飞很远；普通的人伴随着贤人，品格自然就会高尚。比喻接近善类，自然就会习染为善。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Luánfèng" are legendary birds of the phoenix type. An ordinary bird following in the wake of a phoenix can fly far; an ordinary person keeping company with the wise will naturally become noble in character. Associating with good people naturally leads one to become good.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 井杆可以扶起来，但井绳却不行。比喻扶持人要扶持那些有能力自强自立的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A well-sweep can be propped upright, but a well-rope cannot. When helping others stand on their own, support those who have the capacity for self-reliance.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 宁可掌管千军万马，也不愿掌管个自由散漫的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One would rather command a thousand troops than manage a single undisciplined person.

PROVERB: 宁可信其有，不可信其无
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指对于某些流言，宁可相信并可以做好准备应付。比喻对出现的事要做到有备无患。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Regarding certain rumors, it is better to believe them and prepare accordingly. One should always be prepared for what may come.

PROVERB: 宁给饥人一口，不给富人一斗
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 斗：容量单位，十升为一斗。指应资助急需帮助的人。喻指要济穷不济富。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Dǒu" is a unit of volume; ten shēng make one dǒu. One should aid those in urgent need. Help the poor, not the rich.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻宁可用难于驾驭的英才，也不用懒散无用的庸才。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): It is better to employ brilliant but difficult-to-manage talent than lazy and useless mediocrities.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 宁可牺牲千军万马，也不可以丢弃一寸土地。指维护国家领土的完整重于一切。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One would rather sacrifice a thousand soldiers than surrender a single inch of territory. Safeguarding national territorial integrity is paramount above all else.

PROVERB: 宁绕十步远，不走一步险
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 宁可绕着走远路，也不贪图近而走险路。指旅行或行军要把安全放在首位。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): It is better to take a longer detour than to risk a dangerous shortcut. Safety must come first in travel or military marches.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指宁可别人辜负我，我不能辜负别人。比喻品德高尚的人不会做对不起别人的事。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): One would rather be let down by others than let others down. A person of noble character would never wrong another.

PROVERB: 宁为太平犬，莫作离乱人
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 宁可做太平盛世的狗，也不做乱世中流离失所的人。指如果人生活在乱世，还不如狗。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): It is better to be a dog in a peaceful era than a displaced refugee in times of chaos. In turbulent times, a person's life is worse than a dog's.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 鸡口：鸡进食的器官。牛后：牛的肛门。比喻宁可在一个小的集体内当家作主，也不愿在一个大集体里任人指挥摆布。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Chicken's beak" is the organ through which a chicken feeds; "ox's rear" is the anus of an ox. It is better to be master of a small group than to be ordered about in a large one.

PROVERB: 宁在直中取，不向曲中求
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 直：正直，正当。曲：弯曲，不正。指宁可走正当的途径去取得，也不愿走不正当的后路去求取。比喻正直的人做事走光明大道，不走歪门邪道。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Zhí" means upright and proper; "qū" means crooked and improper. It is better to obtain something through proper channels than to seek it through underhanded means. An upright person takes the open road, never the crooked path.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 反：同"返"。首：头指向的方向。指鸟虽然飞得远，终究还是要返回旧巢；狐狸死时，总是把头朝着自己居住的山丘。比喻不忘本。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Fǎn" is the same as "return"; "shǒu" refers to the direction one's head faces. Though a bird may fly far, it ultimately returns to its old nest; when a fox dies, its head always faces toward the hill where it lived. This means never forgetting one's origins.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 喻指互争高低。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Refers to competing with each other for superiority.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时认为如果妻子比丈夫大三岁，丈夫的家业就会旺盛。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times it was believed that if a wife was three years older than her husband, the family's fortunes would prosper.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 和尚：出家修行的男性佛教徒。庙：寺庙。指和尚逃跑了，寺庙不可能跑。比喻无法逃脱。换句话说，人可以跑掉，家产跑不掉，其他有牵连的人也不可能走掉。暂时应急的手段只能躲避一时，但最终还是逃脱不掉。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Monk" refers to a male Buddhist who has renounced worldly life; "temple" refers to a monastery. The monk may run away, but the temple cannot. There is no ultimate escape. A person may flee, but property and associates cannot all disappear. Temporary expedients may provide momentary refuge, but in the end one cannot escape.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 一个人如果舍身拼命，再勇敢的将士也抵挡不住。意思是不怕死的人最勇敢。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If one person fights with complete disregard for life, even the bravest generals cannot withstand them. Those who do not fear death are the most courageous of all.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 批：刮。捋：用手握住向另一端滑动。指刮龙的鳞片不难，摸老虎的胡须却难。又指皇帝是真龙天子，敢于苴言规劝；权臣好比老虎，不敢顶撞得罪。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Pī" means to scrape; "lǚ" means to slide one's grip along something. Scraping a dragon's scales is not difficult, but stroking a tiger's whiskers is. The emperor, being the true dragon and Son of Heaven, can be admonished with frank counsel; but a powerful minister is like a tiger — one dares not offend him.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 便宜：好处，利益。过：错过。当家：本家,自家。指利益不能落到不担干系的人手中。换句话说，有好处要让自己人受益，不能便宜了别人.
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Piányi" means benefit or advantage; "guò" means to miss or pass by; "dāngjiā" means one's own family. Benefits must not fall into the hands of those who bear no responsibility. In other words, advantages should benefit one's own people and not be given away to outsiders.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 便宜：实惠好处。指得便宜的事只能落在自家人手里。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Piányi" means practical benefit. Advantages should only go to one's own people.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 偏听偏信，导致产生邪恶的人；独断专行，容易造成混乱的局面。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Listening only to one side leads to the rise of evil people; acting dictatorially easily creates chaotic situations.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻纠纷或争斗突然发生。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A metaphor for a dispute or conflict erupting suddenly and unexpectedly.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻就在身边，却到处寻找。也比喻同时干两项工作。还比喻在保住已到手的地位或利益的同时，寻找更好的去处。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A metaphor for something being right at hand yet searching everywhere for it. Also describes doing two things simultaneously, or seeking better opportunities while holding onto what one already has.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 下棋时碰到高手，打仗时遇到良将。意指双方力量才智差不多。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Meeting a master at chess; encountering a fine general in battle. Both sides are roughly equal in strength and wit.

PROVERB: 棋逢对手难相胜，将遇良才不敢骄
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指强者遇到强者，难以取胜，彼此不敢相互轻视。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When a strong player meets another strong player, neither can easily prevail, and neither dares look down upon the other.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 着：下棋时走一步或下一子称"一着" 。缚：捆绑。指同棋艺高的人下棋，总感觉手脚如同被捆住了一样，水平不能发挥。换句话说，跟实力高于自己的对手竞争，明显处于劣势，感觉受到约束限制，才能施展不出来。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Zhāo" in chess means one move or placing one piece. "Fù" means to bind. Playing against a superior chess player, one always feels as though one's hands and feet are tied and cannot perform at one's best. Competing against someone stronger than oneself, one is clearly at a disadvantage, feeling constrained and unable to display one's true abilities.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 战旗一展开就取得了胜利，战马到就取胜。意指事情发展迅速顺利。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The battle flag unfurls and victory is won; the war horse arrives and triumph follows. Things develop swiftly and smoothly.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指古时官场积弊根深蒂固，很难改变。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The deep-rooted corruption of ancient officialdom was extremely difficult to change.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 招募一千个士兵不难，求得一个将领却很难。指优秀的将领不容易求得。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Recruiting a thousand soldiers is not difficult, but finding one good general is. Excellent commanders are hard to come by.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 即使有千条错万条错，被派来谈判的人本身是没有过错的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Even if there are a thousand wrongs and ten thousand errors, the person sent to negotiate bears no fault in themselves.

PROVERB: 千锤成利器，百炼成纯钢
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 锋利的刀剑是锤打出来的，成色好的钢是反复炼制而成的。意指人的技能须经过反复磨炼才能获取。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A sharp blade is hammered into shape; fine steel is forged through repeated smelting. A person's skills must be refined through repeated practice and tempering.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻人们纷纷议论的时候，由一人作出最后决定，也叫千人打鼓，锤定音。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When many people are discussing and debating, one person makes the final decision — also called "a thousand people beat the drum, but one hammer strike sets the tone."

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻回顾反思有好处，做过的事情要及时总结经验教训，发扬优点纠正错误，有利于下一步改进工作方法，提高工作质量。换句话说，及时回顾、反思 、总结往事，受益匪浅。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Looking back and reflecting is beneficial. One should promptly review past actions, draw lessons from experience, carry forward strengths, correct mistakes, and thereby improve working methods and raise the quality of work. In other words, timely reflection and summarization of the past yields great benefit.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指社会安定最为可贵难得。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Social stability is the most precious and rare of things.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指在作战时离间双方相当重要千口吃饭，主事一人意思是一个团体中总得有一个管事的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In warfare, driving a wedge between the two sides is critically important. "A thousand mouths to feed, but one person manages affairs" — in any group there must be someone in charge.

PROVERB: 千里不同风，百里不共雷
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 千里之内不会吹相同方向吹来的风，百里之内也不会同响一声雷。意思指地域不一样，风俗、事物也各不一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Within a thousand lǐ, the wind does not blow from the same direction; within a hundred lǐ, thunder does not sound the same. Different regions have different customs and conditions.

PROVERB: 千里不同风，百里不同俗
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 千里之内不会吹相同风向的风百里之内也不存在完全一样的风俗习惯。意指地域不一样，风俗迥异。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Within a thousand lǐ, the wind does not blow the same way; within a hundred lǐ, customs are never exactly alike. Different regions have vastly different customs.

PROVERB: 千里馈粮，士有饥色；樵苏后炊，师不宿饱
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 馈粮：运输粮食。樵苏：打柴割草。宿饱：晚饭吃得饱，到第二天晨还不饿。指千里运粮，士兵们显出饥饿的脸色；打下柴草再做饭，队伍里不可能有隔夜饱。也指后勤供给困难，就会影响到士兵们的健康状况与精神风貌。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Kuìliáng" means transporting grain; "qiáosū" means gathering firewood and cutting grass; "sùbǎo" means eating a full dinner that lasts until the next morning. Transporting grain over a thousand lǐ leaves soldiers looking hungry; if they must gather firewood before cooking, the army can never be full from the previous night's meal. Difficult logistics will affect soldiers' health and morale.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意谓千里去做官，图的是吃好穿好。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Traveling a thousand lǐ to take up an official post, the aim is simply to eat well and dress well.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指野猪寿命再长，最后还是被老虎吃掉了。喻指弱者始终逃脱不掉被强者吞食的命运。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter how long a wild boar lives, in the end it is devoured by the tiger. The weak can never ultimately escape being consumed by the strong.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指年代巳久的字据、协约就是凭证。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Documents and agreements that have stood for a long time serve as proof and evidence.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 赊：赊欠，延期交付。现：现金。指卖东西时赊欠一千块钱，还不如现场交清八百块钱划算。喻指实实在在地现场得到好处，比后来预期的好处更为可信。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Shē" means to buy on credit with deferred payment; "xiàn" means cash. Selling something for a thousand on credit is not as good as receiving eight hundred in cash on the spot. Tangible benefits received now are more reliable than expected benefits in the future.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 一千个人领唱，上万个人就响应起来合唱。意指响应的人很多。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A thousand people begin to sing, and ten thousand join in chorus. Many people respond and follow.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 还：偿付。指很多人买药，让一个人来结账。也指让一个人回报大家所得到的好处。比喻大家得到的好处，都是因为同一个人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Huán" means to repay. A thousand people buy medicine but have one person settle the bill. Also means having one person repay the benefits received by all. Everyone's gains come from the same source.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 在团体演奏中，总得有一个人担任指挥。意谓大家意见再多，总得有一个最后拍板的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In an ensemble performance, there must be one conductor. No matter how many opinions there are, someone must have the final say.

PROVERB: 千人诺诺，不如一士谔谔
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 很多人唯唯诺诺非常顺从，远比不上有一个人能直言争辩。意谓要善于听取不同的意见。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A thousand people nodding in agreement is far less valuable than one person who dares to speak frankly and argue. One should be willing to listen to dissenting opinions.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 长期练兵是为了情况紧急时派上用场。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Training soldiers over a long period is for the purpose of deploying them when urgent need arises.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指听上一千次，比不上亲眼看见一次真实可靠。喻指亲身观察体会远比道听途说好。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Hearing something a thousand times is not as reliable as seeing it once with one's own eyes. Personal observation and experience are far superior to hearsay.

PROVERB: 千羊在望，不如一兔在手
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 在望：视线以内，能够看见。指眼前有一千只羊，也不能与实际得到的一只兔子相比。喻指末来有可能获得很多的好处，也不如已经到手的好处实惠。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Zàiwàng" means within sight, visible. Even a thousand sheep before one's eyes cannot compare with one rabbit actually in hand. Future potential gains, no matter how great, are not as practical as benefits already secured.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指临阵打仗，头阵影响非常大，不得不打好。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In battle, the first engagement has enormous impact and must be fought well.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意指人窝囊没有出息，对他施加压力也不管用。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If a person is spineless and lacks ambition, applying pressure on them is useless.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指前人辛辛苦苦种树，得益的是后人。比喻前人为后人造福。换句话说，前一辈人创业，后一代人便可享福。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): The previous generation toils to plant trees so that later generations may enjoy the shade. The predecessors create blessings for those who come after. The older generation establishes the enterprise; the younger generation reaps the benefits.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 用强硬的手段差遣将领参战比不上激将之法管用。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Using force to order generals into battle is less effective than using the strategy of provocation to motivate them.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 英勇的将领手下没有怯懦的士兵。意谓能干的人手下没有弱者。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Under a brave general there are no cowardly soldiers. A capable leader has no weak followers.

PROVERB: 强迫不成买卖，强求不成夫妻
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指如果用强迫的手段，很难办成事情。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If compulsion is used, it will be very difficult to accomplish anything.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻互不牵连，分得十分清楚。换句话说，完全相反的事物，不可以混淆在一起。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A metaphor for things being completely unrelated and clearly separated. Completely opposite matters must not be confused with one another.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指古时清官受到金钱的诱惑，也会下水，做不到底。也指清官不同流合污，必受到同僚嫉妒，保不住官位。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times, even upright officials could be tempted by money and "fall into the water," unable to remain clean to the end. Also, an official who refuses to go along with corruption will be resented by colleagues and may not keep their position.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 清正廉洁的官员很难被贪赃枉法的属吏所蒙蔽。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): A truly honest and upright official is difficult for corrupt subordinates to deceive.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指无论官员多么清正廉明，最终也逃脱不了奸猾下属的陷阱。喻指官员自己虽然很想清廉，但最终受到属吏的蒙蔽，被拉下水去，还是做了贪官。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No matter how upright an official may be, they ultimately cannot escape the traps set by cunning underlings. Though the official personally wishes to remain clean, they are eventually deceived by subordinates, dragged down, and become corrupt themselves.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 实际上是自己吃自己的东西。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In reality, one is eating one's own food — spending one's own resources.

PROVERB: 晴天开水道，须防暴雨时
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 晴天开水沟目的是为了下暴雨时排水畅通。意指遇到事情要提前做好准备。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Digging drainage ditches on sunny days ensures that when heavy rain comes, water flows away smoothly. One must prepare in advance for problems.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 激将军出马比请将军出马更管用。也泛指求人做事，正言恳求比不上反话激他。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Provoking a general into action is more effective than politely requesting their service. More broadly, when asking someone to do something, reverse psychology works better than earnest, straightforward entreaty.

PROVERB: 请来镇山神，不怕妖作怪
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 比喻有了可以依靠的力量，就不恐惧与自己作对的力量。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Once one has a reliable force to depend on, one need not fear opposing forces.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 对于溃败的残敌，不要逼得太紧，防止其反扑，造成更大的损失。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Do not press a defeated and retreating enemy too hard, lest they turn and counterattack, causing even greater losses.

PROVERB: 曲木恶直绳，重罚恶朋证
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 曲木：弯曲的木头。恶：憎恶，害怕。直绳：木匠用来打直线的墨绳。重罚：指受到严厉惩处。明证：确凿的证据。指曲木惧怕用墨线来衡量罪犯惧怕用确凿的证据来定罪。比喻行为不轨、为非作歹的人畏惧严明公正的法律。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Qūmù" means crooked wood; "wù" means to fear; "zhíshéng" is the carpenter's ink line used to draw straight lines; "zhòngfá" means severe punishment; "míngzhèng" means solid evidence. Crooked wood fears the ink line's measure; criminals fear being convicted on solid evidence. Those who behave crookedly and commit evil deeds fear strict and just law.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 用拳头打人时往往会造成对方受伤。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Striking someone with a fist often results in injury to the other party.

PROVERB: 让一让二，不能让三让四
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 忍让是有一定限度的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Tolerance and forbearance have their limits.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指一个人如果犯法，按道理应该受到法律制裁。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): If a person breaks the law, they should by rights face legal punishment.

PROVERB: 人不害人身不贵，火不烧山地不肥
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 古时指人必须通过损害别人的利益才能攀附上高贵的地位。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): In ancient times it was said that one must harm others' interests in order to climb to a position of high status.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 人不可能十全十美，就同瓜没有绝对的圆一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): No person can be perfect in every way, just as no melon is perfectly round.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指人不愿意离开自己的家乡，就像鸟儿离不开树枝一样。说明人们都留恋自己的故土。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): People are unwilling to leave their homeland, just as birds cannot leave their branches. This illustrates how people are attached to their native soil.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指看一个人不能光凭他嘴上说得好，如同看一条狗不能光看尾巴摇得欢一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When judging a person, one cannot rely solely on their fine words, just as when judging a dog, one cannot rely solely on how eagerly it wags its tail.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 意思是人多智谋多，集中大家的智慧就会如有韩信那样的才能一样。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): When many people pool their wisdom, together they can match the genius of Han Xin. Collective intelligence is formidable.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指众人中肯定有德高望重的人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Among a multitude of people, there are surely those of great virtue and high prestige.

PROVERB: 人恶人怕天不怕，人善人欺天不欺
EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指恶入虽然猖狂，让人畏惧，但老天爷不怕他；善良的人虽然受欺侮，但老天爷不欺负他。比喻天道公平，恶人必受惩罚，好人得到庇护换句话说，上天是公平的，不偏袒恶人也不欺负好人。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): Though a wicked person may be fearsome and rampant, Heaven does not fear them; though a kind person may be bullied, Heaven does not bully them. Heaven is fair: the wicked are punished and the good are protected. In other words, Heaven is impartial — it neither favors the wicked nor oppresses the good.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指人每逢过年过节时，都会情不自禁地更加想念自己远方的亲人或朋友。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): During festivals and holidays, people cannot help but miss their distant relatives and friends all the more.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 见机：看机会,看形势。指人的难得之处在于能够做到见机行事。换句话说，人能够做到见机行事是最为难得的。
EXPLANATION (ENGLISH): "Jiànjī" means to read the situation and seize the opportunity. What is most admirable in a person is the ability to act according to circumstances. In other words, the ability to adapt one's actions to the situation is a most rare and valuable quality.

EXPLANATION (ORIGINAL LANGUAGE): 指人的难得之处在于对自己有个合适的评价。
